title: The anxiolytic-like effect of the aqueous extract of Punica granatum depends on the stress level of fish and mice: Evidence of a homeostatic re-establishing effect
abstract: Pomegranate (Punica granatum) has shown potential anxiolytic and antidepressant effects in preclinical research, but its mechanisms remain unclear. Importantly, some evidence suggests that the effects of P. granatum depend on previous stress, suggesting an adaptogenic effect. This study aimed to evaluate the anxiolytic-like effects of an aqueous extract of P. granatum (AE-PG) on lambaris and zebrafish exposed to acute restraint stress (ARS) and female BALB/c mice exposed to unpredictable chronic mild stress (CUMS). In addition, we evaluated antidepressant-like effects in female BALB/c mice. Acute administration of AE-PG (1 mg/kg, i.p.) was tested in the novel tank test (NTT) in lambaris and zebrafish and in the light/dark test (LDT) in zebrafish, while chronic (7 days) administration of AE-PG (1 mg/kg, i.p.) was tested in the elevated plus-maze (EPM), open-field test (OFT), splash test (ST), and forced swim test (FST) in mice. ARS increased geotaxis and erratic swimming in the NTT, as well as scototaxis, risk assessment, and erratic swimming in the LDT. Acute pre-treatment with AE-PG blocked the effects of ARS on these anxiety-like endpoints in both lambaris and zebrafish. CUMS increased open arm avoidance in the EPM, thigmotaxis and horizontal and vertical exploration in the OFT, and immobility in the FST, and decreased grooming in the ST. Chronic treatment with AE-PG blocked the effects of CUMS on anxiety-like endpoints, and depression-like endpoints, in mice. An in silico analysis of the main compounds in AE-PG suggested a possible mechanism of action on a wide network of targets that converge on PI3K/Akt and show differential expression in brain regions associated with fear- and anxiety-like behavior. Molecular docking suggests that a compound from AE-PG, ellagic acid, is likely to act through estrogen receptors, which could help reestablish homeostatic balance in response to stress.

title: Broadband radio-frequency TEM specimen holders for in situ biasing excitation and 100-ps-scale electron beam control
abstract: Broadband electrical excitation inside a transmission electron microscope (TEM) is required to investigate electrically driven nanodevices at their actual operating frequencies and to develop fully electrical time-resolved experiments at a sub-nanosecond range. Here, we report the performances of homemade two- and four-channel radio-frequency (RF) TEM specimen holders based on a hybrid architecture combining coaxial transmission lines with miniaturized impedance-controlled printed circuit boards (PCB). Removable mechanical contacts provide direct electrical connection to interchangeable TEM chips without wire bonding. Vector network analyzer measurements demonstrate broadband transmission through the complete electrical path up to the specimen. With a representative TEM chip, the two-channel holder exhibits a -3 dB bandwidth of 7.9 GHz, while insertion losses remain below 12 dB up to 18 GHz. The same RF holder architecture was used to drive a miniaturized electrostatic electron-beam deflector. The measured temporal response indicates that the holder deflector assembly remains compatible with electrical pulse durations approaching 100 ps, with the shortest accessible times presently limited by the available waveform generator. High-resolution TEM imaging with a 200 ps probe window does not show detectable degradation of spatial resolution, while off-axis electron holography is successfully performed for probe durations down to 0.5 ns under conditions representative of operando measurements. These results establish a versatile broadband platform combining GHz electrical excitation and sub-nanosecond electron-beam control. The dual-stage configuration of our Hitachi HF3300 microscope further provides the basis for a future fully electrical pump-probe TEM approach using independently driven RF holders for specimen excitation and electron-probe control.

title: Energy Flow Shapes the Decomposition Dynamics of a Reactive Atmospheric Intermediate
abstract: The unimolecular dynamics of Criegee intermediates depend strongly on their internal energy, which can differ substantially between nascent atmospheric species and laboratory-prepared reactants. Here, the decomposition dynamics of {\it anti-}CH$_3$CHOO are investigated using molecular dynamics simulations on a neural network-based potential energy surface under thermal and mode-selective vibrational excitation. Simulations were performed at internal energies representative of those released during ozonolysis (chemical/thermal preparation, TP) or following vibrational excitation (VibEx) along the CH-stretching mode with two or three quanta, as can be done in laboratory studies. These excitation conditions strongly affect reaction yields and kinetics, with VibEx promoting passage across the initial cyclization barrier. For TP, 35 kcal/mol of internal energy are required to form molecular products, whereas for VibEx, 27 kcal/mol are sufficient. Although TP and VibEx ensembles access largely the same fragmentation pathways with comparable relative yields, the absolute product yields, characteristic timescales, and kinetic behavior differ substantially. Methyldioxirane is found to be a kinetic trap along the pathway. The resulting molecular-level description of {\it anti-}CH$_3$CHOO decomposition provides guidance for interpreting experiments and contributes to a broader understanding of energy-dependent Criegee-intermediate dynamics.

title: Poisoning the corpora of protein design systems during pre-training and retrieval
abstract: Protein foundation models increasingly support the generation of novel biological sequences, yet their reliance on large public datasets creates opportunities for adversarial manipulation of the material they learn from and retrieve. We investigate two data-only poisoning attacks against protein design systems, targeting the pre-training corpus of autoregressive protein language models and the retrieval corpus of a text-guided protein generator. For the first, we pre-trained ProtGPT2 and ProGen2 variants of 300 million parameters, introducing poisoned protein sequences containing one of two triggers followed by one of three payloads. Across all poisoned runs, both architectures acquired highly reliable trigger-dependent generation under uniform and ramped poisoning schedules. Under ramped exposure, the earliest majority activation occurred after only 200 contaminated examples, while for the uniform schedule earliest activation occurred around 5000 poisoned samples. For the second attack, we inserted records into a retrieval corpus system without modifying its weights or decoding procedure. A single query-aware record captured a top-16 retrieval position for 58\% of templated requests and 97\% of free-text requests. Conditional on successful poisoned retrieval, 62\% of requests produced altered sequences, while 19-21% acquired the inserted domain by profile-HMM homology. A universal query-unaware attack using 1,500 records also achieved substantial retrieval capture and domain transfer. Together, these findings demonstrate that adversarial protein sequence contributions can establish persistent, sequence-specific behaviour during pre-training or redirect protein generation at inference, while leaving ordinary model behaviour largely preserved. Our work establishes the integrity and biological provenance of protein sequence data as critical safeguards for generative protein design systems.

title: Visualizing B–N Bond Breaking in Silicone Elastomer Networks through Turn-On Mechanochromic Luminescence
abstract: Mechanochromic luminescence (MCL) plays important roles in sensors, encryption, as impact indicators, and in real-time stress mapping. Boron–nitrogen Lewis pairs (LPs) are promising as mechanophores because both the interaction energy and the luminescence color can be readily fine-tuned. However, elastomers based on luminescent organoboron polymers have yet to be explored. Mechanofluorochromic elastomers were prepared by cross-linking pyridyl-substituted poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) with luminescent polystyrene (PS)-based organoborane polymeric Lewis acids. Apart from enabling the full compatibilization of otherwise immiscible PS/PDMS matrices, supramolecular B–N bond formation quenched the blue emission of PS1 via complexation of its pendant bithiophenyl-substituted arylborane chromophore units with pyridyl-functionalized PDMS. Upon stretching of the polymer film, a fluorescence turn-on, corresponding to uncomplexed boron chromophores, was observed by the naked eye under UV irradiation, indicating that the mechanical force was effectively translated to cleave the dynamic B–N bond. Aided by the low Tg of the PDMS segments, the “frustrated” mechanofluorochromic Lewis pairs (MFLPs) recombined instantly upon stress relief, rendering the material nonfluorescent again. Use of a yellow-luminescent donor-π-acceptor fluorophore that turns blue-emissive after pyridyl binding in PS2 led to a ratiometric fluorescence response. Tensile tests and oscillatory rheology studies showed that network F1 was relatively stronger than network F2, consistent with the relative Lewis acid strengths and ligand exchange kinetics derived from studies on molecular model systems. These results demonstrate the potential of tunable B–N Lewis pairs as versatile mechanofluorochromic cross-links in polymer networks.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Autonomous Biogenesis of Early and Late Assembly Intermediates of a Large Ribosomal Subunit in a Minimal System
abstract: Cell-free autonomous biogenesis of ribosomes is important for the bottom-up assembly of an artificial cell and for engineering of functional ribosomes with novel activities. The challenge lies in establishing conditions for a single-step multicomponent synthesis and assembly process in a minimal transcription–translation reaction. We previously reported autonomous synthesis and assembly of a bacterial small ribosomal subunit, but the assembly pathway of the large subunit is more complex with dozens of proteins that bind, fold, and chemically modify its ∼3000-base-long rRNA (rRNA). Here, we cosynthesized all the large subunit components including 33 ribosomal proteins (r-proteins) and 2 rRNAs from DNA brushes and followed the dynamics of assembly coupled to synthesis in real time using total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy. A systematic screen of the binding of each of the ribosomal proteins to the 23S rRNA revealed an assembly pattern indicative of early intermediates. The addition of genes coding for six rRNA assembly factors facilitated binding of late assembly ribosomal proteins, supporting formation of late-stage intermediates even in the absence of rRNA modifications. We established a scenario for the large subunit biogenesis via macromolecular colocalization that may aid in the identification and characterization of additional genes required for achieving complete functional ribosome self-regeneration in a minimal system.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Tuning Second-Sphere Amine Basicity to Modulate Hydride Intermediates and Selectivity in Molecular Manganese Bipyridine CO2 Electroreduction
abstract: Manganese bipyridine tricarbonyl complexes represent a prominent class of molecular electrocatalysts for efficient and selective CO2-to-CO conversion. Recent efforts have sought to redirect product selectivity toward HCOOH by incorporating second-sphere amine proton relays. However, how the physicochemical properties of second-sphere amines govern catalytic activity and selectivity remains insufficiently understood.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Functionalized Olefin-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks for Selective Mercury Capture and Recovery from Vinyl Chloride-Rich Gas Streams
abstract: The calcium carbide-derived acetylene hydrochlorination route for vinyl chloride monomer (VCM, C2H3Cl) production remains a major source of mercury consumption and emission owing to its reliance on HgCl2/activated carbon catalysts. Selective removal of elemental mercury (Hg0) from crude VCM streams is intrinsically challenging because Hg0 must be captured from C2H3Cl-rich and HCl-containing atmospheres without coadsorbing valuable C2H3Cl.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Constrained Nuclear-Electronic Orbital Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory for Excited-State Dynamics with Nuclear Quantum Effects
abstract: Nuclear quantum effects can strongly influence excited-state processes involving light nuclei, yet their inclusion in practical molecular dynamics remains challenging. We develop constrained nuclear-electronic orbital time-dependent density functional theory (CNEO-TDDFT), which incorporates quantum-nuclear delocalization into full-dimensional effective excited-state potential energy surfaces while retaining the formal structure and computational scaling of conventional TDDFT. Analytic gradients are also developed, enabling efficient on-the-fly excited-state dynamics. CNEO-TDDFT substantially improves excited-state vibrational frequencies involving hydrogen motion and reduces the root-mean-square deviation from experiment from 113 cm$^{-1}$ to 26 cm$^{-1}$. For excited-state proton transfer in 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline (HBQ), CNEO-TDDFT yields a characteristic transfer time of 14.0 fs, compared with 25.5 fs from conventional TDDFT, consistent with the experimentally inferred ultrafast timescale of 12$\pm$6 fs. These results establish CNEO-TDDFT as an accurate and efficient framework for excited-state dynamics with nuclear quantum effects.

title: Noise-Space Reward Alignment for Few-Step Generative Models
abstract: Few-step generative models produce high-quality samples in one or a few evaluations. However, steering them toward desired properties remains difficult, especially when only black-box reward evaluations are available. While one could apply approaches developed for iterative diffusion and flow-based models, such as direct RL fine-tuning or test-time scaling, we find that neither transfers well to the few-step regime: direct fine-tuning suffers from severe reward over-optimization, and test-time scaling sacrifices the efficiency advantage of few-step generation. We propose Noise Policy Optimization (NPO), which explicitly targets the alignment problem for few-step generative models. The key idea is to learn an amortized flow policy over the initial noise space of the generator. The trained policy transports Gaussian noise to a reward-tilted noise distribution, whose pushforward distribution through the frozen generator is exactly the reward-tilted output distribution. By keeping the generator frozen, we can effectively utilize the knowledge encoded in the pretrained model, yielding a better reward-quality trade-off than direct fine-tuning. The amortized policy moves the search cost into training, so inference adds only a lightweight noise sampling step on top of the pretrained model. To improve sample efficiency during training, we use ELBO-based likelihood estimation that requires only sampled endpoints rather than simulated trajectories. Across image, language, and protein structure generation, NPO consistently achieves a better reward-quality trade-off than direct fine-tuning, and matches test-time search methods with 16 to 549 times lower inference cost.

title: Predicting Live Birth After Fresh Embryo Transfer in IVF/ICSI: Differential ICM/Trophectoderm Morphology Encoding and a Hybrid Attention--Logistic Regression Ensemble
abstract: Predicting live birth before fresh embryo transfer could support shared decision-making in IVF/ICSI, but routine clinical data are small, heterogeneous, and contain pathway-dependent variables prone to outcome leakage. We aimed to construct a curated single-centre IVF/ICSI dataset and develop a prediction model suited to small tabular clinical data. \textit{Materials and Methods:} We assembled 616 fresh embryo-transfer cycles (251 live birth, 365 non-live birth) with clinical, laboratory, and embryological predictors, and embryo morphology encoded with a novel differential weighting of the inner cell mass and trophectoderm. After KNN imputation, robust scaling, and selection of 50 features, we developed a Hybrid Attention Network (HAN), a learnable feature-attention gate followed by a compact multilayer perceptron, and a HAN + logistic-regression (LR) ensemble with a validation-tuned weight. Models were benchmarked against classical machine learning, TabPFN, and text-serialized language models on a held-out test set; AUC-ROC was the primary metric. \textit{Results:} The HAN + LR ensemble achieved the highest test AUC-ROC (0.710; accuracy 0.710, F1 0.630), ahead of the HAN backbone alone (0.700), logistic regression (0.667), the TabPFN + LR hybrid (0.666), and TabPFN (0.650). Text-serialized language models performed near chance (AUC $\le$ 0.61). The differentially weighted trophectoderm feature ranked highest by consensus importance across models. \textit{Discussion:} A compact attention network combined with a linear model outperformed both components and strong foundation-model baselines on a small clinical cohort. \textit{Conclusion:} The curated dataset and HAN + LR ensemble offer a transparent, reproducible basis for IVF/ICSI live-birth prediction; external validation is the next step.

title: Machine learning and network pharmacology-assisted discovery of natural product inhibitors targeting Plasmodium falciparum lysyl-tRNA synthetase
abstract: The emergence of drug-resistant Plasmodium falciparum necessitates novel antimalarial strategies. Lysyl-tRNA synthetase from Plasmodium falciparum (PfLysRS), an essential enzyme involved in protein biosynthesis, represents a promising molecular target for structure-based drug discovery and development of effective antimalarial agents. In this study, an integrated computational workflow identified three natural product-derived lead compounds, MolPort-001-742-110, MolPort-000-778-336, and MolPort-001-740-194, through structure-based virtual screening with favourable binding affinity and…
venue: SAR and QSAR in environmental research

title: Large Language Model-Assisted Systematic Study of Anomalous Adsorption Phenomena
abstract: Soft porous crystals can undergo guest-induced structural transitions producing unconventional adsorption isotherms, which are valuable for gas separation and storage applications. However, the evidence for these transitions is scattered across the literature in narrative form and has not been aggregated. Here we use a large language model pipeline to mine the literature for anomalous adsorption, extracting phase-transition events together with material, adsorbate, temperature and pressure metadata and classifying each into an established behavioural class. Benchmarked against human annotation, the extraction stage attains an F1 score of 0.96. When applied at scale, the pipeline yields a curated corpus of 547 transitions across 240 distinct materials, drawn from 200 of 4,252 screened publications, which we further link to crystallographic structures. Analysis of this database shows that the principal behavioural classes, gate-opening and breathing, are distinguished by their functional response. Gate-opening frameworks transform at a significantly lower pressure than breathing frameworks (p = 3.8E-3). In contrast, no difference in pore size, void fraction, linker chemistry or metal identity was detected between the classes. Our findings argue for a functional rather than purely structural description of responsive porous materials. They also highlight the need for a community database that records the guest, temperature and pressure of every reported transition of these materials.

title: SALTO: Solver-Anchored Lifted Transfer Operators for Nonlinear Event Inference
abstract: Learned dynamical models can accurately predict trajectories while producing unreliable sensitivities when differentiated or transposed, limiting their use in inverse problems and scientific decision-making. Classical adjoints provide exact local derivatives, but a single adjoint cannot represent the nonlinear response of a system to a family of finite-amplitude perturbations. We introduce SALTO (Solver-Anchored Lifted Transfer Operators), a Koopman-based framework for inferring finite-amplitude sources. In the lifted space, the nonlinear dynamics are approximated by a linear propagator, and its transpose carries each sensor backward in a single solve. The result is a reusable lifted adjoint that predicts the measurement produced by any candidate localized event with one encoder pass and an inner product. To give the model the simulator's exact local behavior, SALTO imposes three structural constraints: it anchors the physical-state dynamics to the simulator's linearized propagator, centers the learned observables so that they vanish to second order at the reference state, and uses a block-triangular lifted propagator. These constraints guarantee that the model reduces to the simulator's tangent dynamics and classical adjoint as the amplitude vanishes, while the learned observables carry only the finite-amplitude correction. On three nonlinear PDE systems, SALTO predicts the measurements of finite-amplitude sources to within 2-8% where the classical adjoint is in error by 41-165%, recovers source position and intensity from sparse sensors nearly as accurately as inversion through the solver, and samples the joint posterior of two interacting sources, matching the solver's posterior on reaction-diffusion at a twentieth of its cost. One trained model serves new sensor layouts and measurement times with a single backward solve.

title: Data-Driven Optimization of Seminumerical Exchange for SIMD CPUs
abstract: We present a seminumerical exchange algorithm (SNK) based on the sn-LinK method [Laqua et al., J. Chem. Theory Comput. 16, 1456 (2020)], optimized for modern multi-core central processing units with single instruction multiple data vector instructions and report its implementation into the Q-Chem quantum chemistry program. Vectorization and memory management strategies for the Boys function and 3-center-1-electron (3c1e) integral kernels are given. Several new considerations are made in the computation of the 3c1e integrals: the Head-Gordon Pople horizontal recurrence relations, same-center optimizations, and multishell optimizations, all implemented symbolically employing the SymPy symbolic algebra library and exported as optimized C++ code leveraging common-sub-expression elimination (CSE) optimization techniques. A general scheme for choosing optimal integral kernels is developed through rigorous timing benchmarks. The resulting implementation is tested against traditional 4c2e exchange for several systems and basis sets, showing 1-2 orders of magnitude speedups for systems of practically relevant sizes (100-500 atoms, 2000-10000 basis functions). For smaller molecules, comparisons are also made against the more efficient occ-RI-K method showing a break-even point around 50-100 atoms beyond which SNK dramatically outperforms due to its superior sub-quadratic (between linear and quadratic) time complexity as well as its effectively negligible memory demand.

title: Machine Learning for Gene-Expression-Based Prediction of Alcohol Use Disorder with an Integrate Web-Based Dashboard
abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a complex condition associated with molecular alterations in brain regions involved in reward, motivation, and behavioral regulation. Gene-expression profiling can provide valuable molecular information for studying AUD; however, the high dimensionality and correlation structure of transcriptomic data present challenges for predictive modeling and interpretation.

title: Quality Assessment and Model Training Impact of Synthetic Images in Medical Diagnostic Imaging: Systematic Review
abstract: BackgroundAI has increasingly been used to generate synthetic images to overcome the scarcity of large, regulatory-compliant medical image datasets. However, their quality and actual utility for algorithm development across deep learning architectures, medical settings, and image types have been poorly assessed.ObjectiveThis study aimed to review the use of synthetic images for algorithm development and to assess their quality and effects on downstream algorithms trained on these images, according to AI architecture, medical setting, and image type.MethodsThe authors conducted a systematic review of studies published between January 2020 and September 2025. PubMed, Scopus, IEEE Xplore, and Embase were searched for peer-reviewed studies evaluating synthetic images generated from human medical imaging data. Data were extracted for imaging modalities, generative architectures, image-quality assessment methods, downstream model performance, explainability approaches, reproducibility practices, and risk of bias. Given substantial heterogeneity and incomplete statistical reporting, findings were synthesized descriptively.ResultsA total of 160 studies were included. Generative adversarial network-based architectures dominated image generation (119 studies, 74.4%), although hybrid and diffusion-based approaches became increasingly represented in recent years. Image-quality evaluation was highly heterogeneous: 50 studies included human-reader evidence, and 101 reported an automated image-quality assessment. Synthetic-only training generally underperformed real-data training, including a median Dice similarity coefficient change of -10.2% for segmentation. Adding synthetic data to real training sets was associated with median improvements in classification precision (+7.8%), recall (+5.3%), F1-score (+5.5%), accuracy (+4.3%), and area under the curve (+4.0%), while the median Dice coefficient improvement was +1.2%. Explainability evidence was reported in 68 (42.5%) studies and was rarely validated against expert annotations. Reproducibility reporting was inconsistent, and only 38% (60/160) of studies were judged to have low overall risk of bias.ConclusionsUnlike previous reviews restricted to particular diseases, imaging modalities, or generative architectures, this review provides a cross-domain quantitative synthesis of both synthetic-image quality assessment and downstream model performance. Synthetic images currently appear more valuable as a complement to real training data than as a replacement, with modest improvements in classification performance, smaller gains in segmentation, and generally poorer performance with synthetic-only training. For researchers, developers, and regulators, these findings highlight the need for standardized multimethod image-quality evaluation, complete reporting, and rigorous external validation before synthetic-image pipelines are translated into clinical AI applications.

title: Integrated identification of CYP1A1 and CYP1B1 as potential drivers of smoking-related lung carcinogenesis
abstract: Smoking is the major environmental risk factor for lung cancer; however, the molecular basis underlying individual susceptibility to smoking-related carcinogenesis remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify smoking-specific molecular signatures associated with lung cancer development and to investigate their potential biological mechanisms. Transcriptomic datasets from smokers with and without lung cancer, as well as never-smokers with lung cancer, were analyzed using differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA).

title: As FDA awaits new chief, concerns rise over role of science advisers
abstract: At a recent confirmation hearing, senators sought assurances from Heidi Overton that advisory committees won’t become another political lever

title: Harnessing Photoexcited-State Pathways in Boron Dipyrromethene for Phototheranostics and Photopolymerization
abstract: Boron dipyrromethene (BODIPY) dyes are widely recognized for their strong visible-light absorption, high fluorescence, and structural modularity. Beyond fluorescence, molecular engineering can redirect their photoexcited states toward distinct photochemical pathways, expanding their utility in photomedicine and materials chemistry. This Spotlight examines BODIPY photochemistry from this excited-state perspective and connects recent advances in phototheranostics and photopolymerization.

title: Solid-state nanopore and nanochannel platforms for biomarker detection in disease diagnosis: recent advances and perspectives
abstract: Solid-state nanopore and nanochannel platforms are versatile label-free biosensors that convert biomolecular transport or binding into ionic current signals. This review organizes recent disease-diagnostic applications around a central design chain. Biomarker properties, including size, charge, conformation, abundance, and sample-matrix context, determine whether direct measurement, a molecular-recognition interface, signal amplification, or structural signal translation is required.

title: Allosteric covalent inhibition of cereblon through cryptic cysteine targeting
abstract: Thalidomide-derived cereblon (CRBN) modulators are among the most clinically impactful targeted protein degradation therapeutics, redirecting the CRL4-CRBN E3 ubiquitin ligase to degrade disease-driving neosubstrates. All current CRBN-targeting IMiDs and CELMoDs engage a single orthosteric pocket, leaving CRBN's conformational landscape largely unexploited pharmacologically. Using cysteine-directed chemoproteomic screening, we identified covalent ligands that engage Cys287, a cryptic allosteric pocket distal to the orthosteric site.

title: Super-Cross-Reactive Recognition Enables Preclinical Diagnosis of Alzheimer’s Disease
abstract: Early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is impeded by the subtle, heterogeneous nature of fluid biomarkers during the disease’s initial phases. Current detection tools, which target single biomarkers, often lack the necessary sensitivity and specificity for presymptomatic screening. To address this, we develop a machine learning-informed supramolecular sensor array that leverages a holistic design to overcome the limitations of “lock-and-key” recognition.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: When Does "Post-Call" Begin? An Availability Contract for Earnings-Call NLP Benchmarks
abstract: Corporate financial disclosures often unfold over time, with announcements, prepared remarks, and discussion spanning multiple high-frequency return intervals. Financial NLP benchmarks can therefore suffer from a within-event timing mismatch when the prediction target begins before the textual or audio input used by a model could be complete. Chronological train--test splits do not prevent this mismatch, because it occurs inside individual events rather than across samples. We introduce an Availability Contract, which requires a benchmark to state the input boundary, evidence for input availability, the outcome start, and the claims supported by that evidence. We apply this framework to 552 earnings calls from 24 firms. For each call, we hold the return endpoint fixed and compare the previous close, a documentary call-start proxy, and a completion proxy based on reconstructed audio end plus a stipulated processing allowance. At this baseline, moving from the call-start proxy to the completion proxy flips return signs for 9.4% of calls. Holding completion-clock cutpoints fixed, 28.3% change quintile. In an independent release-session analysis of a public earnings-call volatility benchmark, shifting before-market target windows forward by one trading session raises three-day mean squared error by 18.1-21.4% across four frozen prediction streams, while their point rankings remain unchanged. Together, the results show that labels and losses can depend materially on the declared outcome clock even when model rankings appear stable. The Availability Contract makes this assumption explicit and ties post-input claims to the available timing evidence.

title: Physics-Informed Deep Learning Surrogate for Mechanical-Response Prediction and Failure Assessment of High-Performance Polymer Composites
abstract: Polymer composites show complex, nonlinear mechanical behaviour. This makes their rational design hard. Running tests or high-fidelity simulations for every candidate design is slow and costly. Purely data-driven models are fast, but they can break basic mechanics outside the training range. Most physics-informed (PI) models, on the other hand, target a single constitutive law or failure mode, and their loss weights are set by hand. This study presents a DBN-GJO-PI-RNN surrogate that links deep feature learning, physics-constrained learning and failure screening in one workflow.

title: High-Resolution 6Li Solid-State Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Reveals Hidden Lithium Dynamics in All-Solid-State Cathodes
abstract: The decisive chemistry of iron-based halide cathodes─where lithium resides, how it evolves, and how disorder governs multielectron redox─has remained largely inaccessible, limiting the rational design of catholyte-free composite cathodes in all-solid-state lithium batteries. Here we make the lithium sublattice directly visible in paramagnetic LiFeCl3 using a 6Li solid-state NMR strategy combining high isotopic enrichment, optimized acquisition, and variable-temperature control.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Network pharmacology and machine learning reveal kit as a target of roburic acid in anaplastic thyroid carcinoma: Preliminary in vitro validation
abstract: This study aims to systematically explore the potential molecular mechanism of Roburic Acid (RBA) in the treatment of Anaplastic Thyroid Carcinoma (ATC) through the approaches of network pharmacology, machine learning and in vitro experiments. Public databases were used to retrieve the potential targets of RBA and disease-related targets of ATC. Intersection analysis was performed to identify the common targets, followed by the construction of a Protein-Protein Interaction (PPI) network for these common targets. Enrichment analyses, including GO functional and KEGG pathway analyses, were carried out for the targets. Core targets were further prioritized using SVM, LASSO and random forest machine learning algorithms. Validation of the binding affinity and stability of RBA with the core target was performed using molecular docking and dynamics simulations. Finally, in vitro experiments-including cell viability, scratch assay, apoptosis detection, and Western blot-were conducted using the ATC cell line KHM-5M to validate the therapeutic effect and underlying mechanism of RBA. A total of 401 RBA-associated targets and 2151 ATC-related targets were identified; their intersection yielded 173 shared targets. GO enrichment analysis indicated that these targets were mainly involved in responses to peptide hormones and nuclear receptor activity, among other biological functions. KEGG pathway analysis showed significant enrichment in cancer-related pathways, including the PI3K-Akt and MAPK signaling pathways. Using SVM, LASSO regression, and random forest models, KIT was consistently identified as the single core target. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated strong binding between RBA and c-KIT, characterized by low binding energy and the formation of a stable protein-ligand complex. In vitro, RBA significantly reduced KHM-5M cell viability and migration; the inhibitory effect on migration became pronounced at 24 h and was comparable to that of the positive control DOX. Furthermore, RBA promoted apoptosis and dose-dependently suppressed c-KIT phosphorylation. This study integrated network pharmacology, machine learning, and molecular simulations to identify KIT as a high-confidence core target of RBA in ATC. Preliminary in vitro validation demonstrated that RBA suppresses ATC cell viability and migration, induces apoptosis, and inhibits c-KIT phosphorylation in a dose-dependent manner.

title: Regioselective and Stereodivergent C–H Functionalization of Internal Alkenes
abstract: Herein, we introduce a new strategy for the regioselective and stereodivergent C–H functionalization of internal alkenes. We discovered that the regioselectivity of internal alkene thianthrenation is exceptionally electronically sensitive and can be controlled by native allylic and homoallylic functional groups. We also found that both alkenyl thianthrenium stereoisomers can be selectively accessed by using different workup conditions. While thianthrenation is typically stereoretentive, the addition of Cs2CO3 in the workup induces isomerization through reversible conjugate addition. We show that both stereoisomers of the alkenyl linchpins can be readily engaged in stereoretentive cross coupling reactions. This selective thianthrenation-coupling sequence introduces a generalizable platform for stereodefined trisubstituted alkene synthesis.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Photocatalytic Three-Component Radical Addition of Aromatic Compounds
abstract: Substitution dominates benzene chemistry because σ-adducts formed during bond construction usually rearomatize. We report a photocatalytic three-component reaction that retains the σ-adduct as a 1,4-dioxygenated cyclohexadiene. A highly reactive carbonyloxy radical adds to the arene, whereas a longer lived peroxyl radical intercepts the resulting cyclohexadienyl radical before rearomatization.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Asymmetric Alkylation of α-Cyanoketimines with Alkyl Bromides Catalyzed by Bis-Cinchonium Salts
abstract: The SN2 reaction constitutes one of the most fundamental bond-forming transformations in organic chemistry, finding numerous synthetic applications across pharmaceutical, agrochemical, and materials science. However, the development of new catalysts for asymmetric SN2 reactions with nucleophiles beyond enolate derivatives remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report the development of a new class of bis-cinchonium catalysts for an unprecedented enantioselective SN2 alkylation of cyanoketimines with alkyl bromides.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Fast3VmrMLM enables statistically powerful and computationally efficient large-scale marker-pair epistasis GWAS in sizable populations
abstract: Identifying marker-pair epistasis in genome-wide association studies remains challenging due to computational burden and statistically underpowered. Hence, we developed a big-data algorithm, Fast3VmrMLM, that integrates a genome-wide pairwise scanning plus machine-learning framework with seven big-data techniques. Fast3VmrMLM considers all possible genetic effects while controlling for all polygenic backgrounds, substantially improving power of identifying epistasis.

title: Unilateral Functionalization of Covalent Organic Frameworks: Local Electronic Modulation and Morphology-Enabled Mass Transport for Electrocatalytic Hydrogen Peroxide Production
abstract: Achieving high selectivity and activity in the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e– ORR) pathway critically depends on the synergistic modulation of a catalyst’s electronic structure and mass diffusion channels. This work proposes an asymmetric modulation strategy via unilateral functionalization, in which −CH3, −CN, −SO3H, and −NO2 moieties are incorporated into a series of covalent organic frameworks (COFs), systematically unraveling the multilevel regulatory mechanisms exerted by functional groups from molecular to macroscopic morphological scales.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Direct Sampling of Nuclear-Quantum Chemical Equilibria by Path-Integral Reaction Ensemble Monte Carlo
abstract: Reaction ensemble Monte Carlo samples chemical composition directly but usually treats the explicit environment with classical nuclei, whereas path-integral methods represent nuclear quantum effects explicitly but generally infer reaction equilibria from partition-function or free-energy ratios between predefined states. We formulate path-integral reaction ensemble Monte Carlo (PI-RxMC), a reaction-constrained expanded ensemble that samples chemical sectors and nuclear paths jointly, and derive the Metropolis-Hastings rule for sector changes, including sector weights, normalization factors…
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Construction of Divergent Enantioenriched 3D-Fluoro Scaffolds via Ni(0) π-Lewis Base-Mediated Umpolung of Fluorodienes
abstract: Enantioenriched three-dimensional (3D) fluorinated scaffolds are pivotal in drug discovery, whereas the asymmetric synthesis directly from readily available 2D fluoroalkenes represents a desirable yet challenging synthetic objective. The α-carbon of gem-difluoroalkenes is inherently electrophilic, which typically precludes their utility in nucleophilic assemblies.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Agentic AIGC: A Survey of Visual Generation Agents
abstract: Visual generation is becoming a general component of AI infrastructure, supporting content creation across design, entertainment, education, science, and industry. Generative and multimodal models have substantially improved single-pass synthesis. At the same time, multi-step visual creation requires spatial precision, identity persistence, temporal coherence, editable structure, factual fidelity, and physical plausibility throughout the creation process. Errors in intermediate artifacts can propagate across subsequent steps, making creation control a central requirement.

title: VoroTypes: automated enumeration of Voronoi cell topologies for structural identification of complex crystals in atomistic simulations
abstract: VoroTypes enumerates, for an arbitrary crystal structure, the complete family of Voronoi cell topologies that can arise under small generic perturbations of atomic positions, and exports it as a topological filter for the VoroTop framework. This extends per-atom structural identification in molecular dynamics simulations, previously limited to a handful of simple reference structures, to complex crystals such as Frank--Kasper and Laves phases, with per-sublattice resolution. The package takes a standard crystallographic description (a CIF or POSCAR file) as input, applies exact symmetry reduction and validity pruning to accelerate the enumeration, and produces filters that load directly into the standalone VoroTop program or into OVITO. A library of pre-computed filters covers over a thousand structures from the Materials Project.

title: Chemical discrimination of wild and cultivated Dendrobium devonianum by ATR-FTIR spectroscopy and machine learning with targeted metabolomic analysis
abstract: Wild and cultivated Dendrobium devonianum are visually similar, but their chemical differences complicate raw-material authentication. Recent spectroscopic studies of Dendrobium have focused primarily on species identification and geographical traceability, with limited chemical interpretation of wild-cultivated discrimination. ATR-FTIR spectroscopy and machine learning were applied to 145 samples (74 wild and 71 cultivated), while targeted metabolomics was performed using six pooled composite samples (three independently prepared pools per group).

title: Excited-State Engineering of Viologen Photocatalysts via Synergistic Through-Space and Through-Bond Electronic Coupling
abstract: Precise manipulation of excited-state charge dynamics represents a fundamental challenge in the molecular design of organic photocatalysts. Herein, we introduce a synergistic electronic coupling strategy for engineering long-lived charge separation states by integrating through-space and through-bond electronic coupling in viologen-based photocatalysts. A family of through-space-conjugated viologens (TSCVs) featuring a dumbbell-shaped donor–acceptor architecture was constructed by integrating extended π-conjugated scaffolds with TSCV units.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Multi-omics atlas of chronic exercise
abstract: Exercise reduces all-cause mortality, yet its molecular effects across organs, sexes, and circadian phases remain incompletely understood. We subjected mice to 8 weeks of voluntary wheel running and collected 22 tissues and plasma during active and inactive phases for bulk RNA sequencing, metabolomics, proteomics, and single-nucleus RNA and methylation sequencing. Exercise induced canonical fiber-type switching and widespread, tissue-specific remodeling, with the largest transcriptomic changes in skeletal muscle. Except for the hypothalamus, kidney, and lung, most tissues changed more during the active phase. Females showed broader transcriptional responses, with distinct downregulation. Pairing single-nucleus methylomes with transcriptomes resolved the cell types driving exercise-induced epigenetic remodeling-changes undetectable by bulk studies. These included coordinated gene-body demethylation and transcription that tracked with fiber-type switching in specific myonuclei. Cell-type-resolved methylation, including partially methylated domains characterized in muscle, revealed a strong, sex-biased epigenetic response to training. Machine learning identified conserved exercise signatures across mammalian species.

title: Interlocked Vortex Order in the Frustrated $A_3$V$_9$Te$_{13}$ Lattice ($A$=Cs,Rb)
abstract: Recently synthesized $A_3$V$_9$Te$_{13}$ ($A$ = Cs, Rb) provides a unique platform for exploring the interplay between geometric frustration, magnetism, and correlated electronic states beyond conventional kagome systems. Based on first-principles calculations, we demonstrate that the frustrated V sublattice naturally stabilizes a robust vortex or anti-vortex antiferromagnetic ground state, whose total energy is substantially lower than all other configurations. In addition, the Heisenberg model analysis show strong constraints on the ground state magnetic configuration, such that fixing spin configuration of 1 triangle propagates and fixes all others. The vortex or anti-vortex phase hosts electronic structures reminiscent of kagome metals, including Dirac-like band crossings, van Hove singularities, and flat bands near the Fermi level. Owing to the noncollinear spin texture and quasi-two-dimensional magnetic character, the Néel temperature exhibits an extremely weak dependence on both the magnitude and direction of external magnetic fields, consistent with experimental observations. For Cs-based compound, the ground state band structure is metallic with 6 Weyl points in the BZ; while for the Rb-based compound, spin--orbit coupling opens an approximately 27-meV gap at ambient pressure due to the lifted C$_3$ symmetry. Our results establish $A_3$V$_9$Te$_{13}$ as a promising platform for studying frustration-driven chiral magnetism and its interplay with topological electronic states.

title: Large in-plane optical anisotropy in epitaxial CrN(113) films
abstract: CrN, a transition-metal nitride crystallizing in the cubic rocksalt structure, exhibits a unique combination of mechanical robustness, semiconducting behavior, and thermoelectric functionality. To date, however, CrN has been synthesized primarily as polycrystalline material or as epitaxial films grown along high-symmetry orientations such as (001) and (111). Here, we prepare epitaxial CrN(113) films on AlN(11\bar{2}2) templates by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy. The low-symmetry interface and highly direction dependent lattice mismatch are expected to modify the physical properties of CrN relative to the bulk material. Indeed, variable-angle spectroscopic ellipsometry in the photon-energy range from 1.25 to 5 eV reveals a surprisingly strong polarization dependence of the optical response despite the nearly strain-free cubic crystal structure of the films. The pseudo-optical constants n and k differ by more than 10% for orthogonal in-plane polarizations throughout the investigated spectral range. We evaluate possible origins of this effect and conclude that it most likely arises from anisotropic surface morphology of CrN(113), which creates a metasurface acting as a subwavelength grating in the strongly absorbing regime.

title: CIM-Embed: Learning Instruction-Conditioned Multimodal Embeddings for Clustering
abstract: Multimodal objects can require different partitions under different instructions, as when products in an e-commerce catalog are grouped by color, material, or both. Retrieval-oriented embeddings may not recover these partitions, while generative clustering often relies on intermediate descriptions or iterative decisions. This paper presents CIM-Embed, a framework for learning instruction-conditioned multimodal embeddings for clustering. Supervised contrastive learning uses same-group positives and negatives from other groups, optionally including other tasks; heterogeneous structured batches accommodate tasks with different group counts. At inference, the model maps each object's image, text, and instruction directly to an embedding; HDBSCAN then forms a partition without the ground-truth cluster count. We construct ProductMIC from product metadata in Amazon Reviews 2023, comprising training data and an evaluation benchmark for instruction-conditioned clustering. The benchmark contains 5,373 products and 449 single-attribute and compositional grouping tasks spanning 50 leaf categories excluded from our training. With full-dimensional embeddings and HDBSCAN, direct within-task SupCon training achieves a mean per-task V-measure of 95.01, compared with 53.06 for WeMM 9B, the strongest general-purpose embedding baseline evaluated. Frozen product-trained encoders also improve out-of-domain conditional grouping, while controlled transfer experiments distinguish partition transfer from instruction response. We will release the code and dataset upon acceptance.

title: Physics-Aware Distillation of a Grid Foundation Model for Real-Time Edge Inference
abstract: Grid foundation models (GridFMs) are graph transformers pretrained on a masked power-flow objective, and evaluate power flow orders of magnitude faster than an iterative solver. Their size, however, targets data-centre inference, whereas low-inertia operation increasingly asks for inference at the edge, next to the measurement, at batch size one and within a single synchrophasor (PMU) reporting frame. We distil a 20.1M-parameter, 12-layer GridFM teacher into a 0.62M-parameter, 6-layer student, a $32.5\times$ parameter reduction at half the message-passing depth, using an objective that combines the masked power-flow loss with output, physics-residual, latent-state and attention transfer. The physics-residual term, which matches the teacher's power-residual profile, has not previously been applied to typed power-grid graphs. We evaluate on a renewable variant of the IEEE 118-bus benchmark grid in which 26 of the conventional (synchronous) generators are replaced by inverter-based renewables with battery flexibility and standardised reactive-power limits (IEEE 1547), giving $97\,529$ physically valid (AC-OPF-feasible) operating scenarios, and we ablate all eight combinations of the transfer terms, reporting accuracy against ground truth and fidelity to the teacher separately. Distillation lowers student error on all four predicted quantities, by up to $48\%$ on active-power dispatch, and every distilled student is more accurate than its teacher on reactive-power dispatch. The gain is largely carried by the output matching term. The physics-residual term, in the layer-aggregated form used here, is consistently harmful, which we attribute to the spatial averaging it applies to a bus-level residual field. The resulting student is $32.5\times$ smaller in parameter count and has half the message-passing depth, making it a candidate for subsequent edge-device benchmarking.

title: Learning the information contained in the microstructure of data distributions
abstract: Understanding how much and where information is nested in sets of data obtained using different parameters and metrics is a typical problem in the analysis of high-dimensional datasets. Approaches based on relative data-driven metrics may be poorly quantitative and difficult to interpret, while accurate methods may be computationally expensive and impractical for large datasets. Here, we report an efficient, quantitative, and transferable method useful to this end, which we call "Micro-Information Analysis". Its foundation is based on the tight relationship that exists between the microscopic features of data distributions and the information they contain. The method performs preliminary unsupervised clustering, capturing microstructural features of data distributions such as the dominant Gaussian microdomains (microstates) present in them, their population, separation, and their residual non-Gaussian fraction. Leveraging the principle of clustering-and-minimization of Shannon entropy, this allows quantifying in bit (that is, in absolute metric) the information contained in the microstructure of the data, and how much information is nested in each Gaussian and non-Gaussian microdomain. The output of the analysis is a set of easily interpretable Information-Microstructure plots that allow to readily compare and rank data based on their information content and to graphically map the information breakdown among their various microenvironments in diagrams that are easy to interpret. We prove the efficiency of our method by analyzing and ranking data generated synthetically or from molecular simulations, demonstrating how "Micro-Information Analysis" is a physically-grounded quantitative tool useful for the study of physical systems from their data and for data science in general.

title: Adding Temperature to the Adiabatic Connection: Hybrid Functionals for Static and Dynamic Correlation
abstract: Capturing static and dynamic electron correlation simultaneously at manageable computational cost remains a key challenge in electronic structure theory. Motivated by the recurring role of effective temperature in self-consistent field methods we extend the adiabatic connection mechanism from density functional theory to include a temperature dimension. This gives rise to thermally enhanced hybrid functionals, in which static correlation is captured via fractional occupations generated by an effective "correlation temperature" within thermal Hartree-Fock, while dynamic correlation is described by established density functional approximations. The framework formally unifies information-density matrix functional theory (i-DMFT) and thermally-assisted-occupation (TAO-)DFT as special cases, clarifying their theoretical basis and the respective prescriptions for the temperature parameter. We assess the performance of several thermally enhanced hybrids for different cases where i-DMFT was previously shown to fail. Furthermore, we discuss and test different schemes for determining the correlation temperature and investigate the accuracy of different such choices for a benchmark set derived from biphenyl. The results help to clarify the achievable balance of accuracy, generality, and efficiency, establishing thermally enhanced hybrids as a systematic route toward low-cost treatment of both correlation types.

title: How Much Physics Can Vision Learn from Audio? Probing and Distilling Damping Structure
abstract: Physical understanding is crucial for decision making, yet vision models struggle to infer properties such as damping that govern how materials behave. Audio encodes such properties directly, because an object's acoustic response to impact reveals its damping through measurable decay. We probe frozen encoders for the quality factor $Q$, a dimensionless measure of how many oscillations an object completes before its ring dies away, and report how well each embedding orders impacts by $Q$ using the Spearman rank correlation $ρ$, for which $ρ=1$ is a perfect ordering and $ρ=0$ an unrelated one. Audio embeddings reach $ρ=0.73$ and retain most of that advantage on materials withheld from training, while a single video frame taken at the moment of impact, encoded by CLIP, supports only $ρ=0.28$. Having established where the signal lives, we ask how much of that gap vision can recover. We distill a frozen audio teacher into a frozen CLIP backbone through a trained projection head and find that this recovers a useful fraction of the audio advantage. Because pooled correlations on this task are dominated in practice by category identity, we also evaluate under a leave-one-material-out protocol in which the held-out material is withheld from the projection head as well as the probe. Distillation with a four-frame input improves the correlation there from 0.234 to 0.338 (+0.053 over the matched four-frame baseline, 14 of 17 materials), a gain that no category-level strategy can produce. Widening the visual input to four frames spanning the impact supplies half of that improvement at no acoustic cost, which indicates that part of what a single frame misses is visible dynamics.

title: Shortcut Sensitivity in Agent-Safety Evaluations
abstract: AI agents take actions through tools. Some actions are sensitive, so guards that supervise them must themselves be evaluated reliably. Yet the data used to evaluate a guard can include cues that make labels predictable without measuring the intended safety construct, and those cues can also influence guard decisions. We introduce a three-level shortcut-auditing framework and audit completed LinuxArena trajectories and two TS-Bench-derived step datasets. We distinguish label predictability, observational guard association, and paired decision sensitivity. In LinuxArena, shorter average shell commands strongly predict trajectory labels. In AgentDojo-Traj, exact-tool lookup falls from F_1=.901 with mixed-domain folds to .495 under domain holdout. In AgentHarm-Traj, released TS-Guard F_1 falls from .902 under row weighting to .719 with equal interaction weighting, while balanced accuracy rises. We then test the strongest safe-row marker association in a seven-configuration screen on a frozen 64-step AgentDojo-Traj cohort using repeated, interleaved Haiku calls. Rewriting the marker lowers blocking by 8.33 percentage points, while opaque tool aliases raise it by 11.46 points. All unsafe calls remain blocked; the changes concern false positives against inherited labels. Both effects remain nonzero after subtracting the formatting-placebo effect, with exploratory 95% ranges excluding zero. The same edits also change measured accuracy against inherited labels. This provides direct evidence that benchmark representation can materially change a guard's decisions and measured evaluation performance. The Haiku-sized effects do not reproduce in Luna or deterministic Q8 TS-Guard. We recommend domain group holdouts, evaluation-unit metrics, and placebo-controlled paired interventions.

title: Pt-induced semimetallic transport and enhanced thermoelectric response in the half-Heusler alloy YNi_{0.5}Pt_{0.5}Bi
abstract: Half-Heusler alloys provide a versatile platform for tuning electronic and thermal transport through chemical substitution. Here, we investigate the thermoelectric and magnetotransport properties of spark-plasma-sintered YNi_{0.5}Pt_{0.5}Bi. Partial substitution of Ni by Pt drives YNiBi toward semimetallic transport, characterized by hole-dominated conduction, a low Hall carrier concentration of $\mathrm{1.9 \times 10^{19} cm^{-3}}$, and a sizeable nonsaturating magnetoresistance of 18$\%$ at 300 K under 14 T. Compared with YNiBi, Pt alloying increases the room-temperature Seebeck coefficient from approximately 90 to 130 $\mathrm{μV K^{-1}}$, while reducing the thermal conductivity to 3.15 $\mathrm{W m^{-1} K^{-1}}$. Single-parabolic-band analysis indicates an enhanced carrier effective mass, resulting in a room-temperature power factor of 13.7 $\mathrm{μW cm^{-1} K^{-2}}$ and a figure of merit ($zT$= 0.13). First-principles calculations further show a Pt-induced closing of the electronic band gap and a low density of states near the Fermi level, consistent with the experimentally observed semimetal-like transport. These results demonstrate that Ni/Pt alloying provides an effective route for simultaneously tuning the electronic, magnetotransport, and thermoelectric properties of YNiBi-based half-Heusler compounds.

title: Global optimization workflow with compact graph neural networks for comprehensive transition-state mapping
abstract: Locating the transition states in them remains a central computational bottleneck, particularly in heterogeneous catalysis where reference data are scarce and the configurations that matter are not known in advance. Most machine-learning approaches to transition-state prediction pursue increasingly expressive architectures trained on abundant gas-phase data, a strategy poorly matched to data-limited surface chemistry.

title: Identification of Cysteine-Reactive Early Mitotic Inhibitors
abstract: Cancer remains a pervasive health problem for millions of Americans, and defining effective anticancer therapeutics remains a major obstacle to the long-term survival of patients. Recent advances in novel chemistries and chemical libraries have enabled researchers to discover and develop covalent inhibitors to treat various diseases, including cancer. This has spurred the generation of cysteine-targeting covalent compound libraries that have not been fully explored within the context of the cell cycle and cell division, which are attractive targets for inhibiting cancer proliferation. We report a novel, cell-based high-content chemical screening strategy for discovering early mitotic spindle assembly inhibitors. We coupled this strategy with a cysteine-reactive covalent compound library containing 3,520 molecules to identify novel early mitotic inhibitors. These inhibitors included a microtubule depolymerizer, a mitotic spindle positioning disruptor, and compounds affecting mitotic spindle structure and chromosome alignment. Two of these compounds triggered mitotic arrest and reduced cell viability at nanomolar concentrations. These inhibitors serve as chemical probes to investigate mechanisms of early cell division and to develop novel cancer therapeutics.

title: Integrating Gaussian Accelerated Molecular Dynamics, β-Variational Autoencoders, and Markov State Models Reveals the Activation Landscape of FGFR3 Kinase
abstract: Fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) kinase plays a crucial role in cellular differentiation, proliferation, and skeletal development. Activation of the kinase domain through phosphorylation regulates the downstream signaling cascades, and its dysregulation leads to human dwarfism, skeletal dysplasia, and multiple cancers. However, the mechanistic basis of FGFR3 regulation by phosphorylation and ligand binding remains unclear. Here, we introduce an integrated GaMD-βVAE-MSM pipeline, a hybrid physics-ML framework for studying kinase activation.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: A novel nitric oxide (NO)-dependent 'molecular switch' mediates LTP in the Octopus vulgaris brain through persistent activation of nitric oxide synthase (NOS)
abstract: Cephalopod mollusks provide a striking example of the independent evolution of advanced cognitive abilities in invertebrates. In octopuses, learning and memory are mediated by the vertical lobe (VL), whose visual input synapses undergo robust activity-dependent long-term potentiation (LTP). Here, we used Octopus vulgaris of either sex to show that persistent activation of nitric oxide synthase (NOS) mediates both LTP expression and maintenance, independently of de novo protein synthesis.
venue: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience

title: From picometre displacements to a three-dimensional lattice gas of polar skyrmions
abstract: Polar skyrmions, the electric analogues of magnetic skyrmions, form arrays in PbTiO3/SrTiO3 superlattices that are known to be only short-range ordered, but how this disordered ensemble is organized in three dimensions, and how its microscopic structure underlies this organization, have remained largely inaccessible. Here, using three-dimensional difference pair distribution function (3D-ΔPDF) analysis of X-ray diffuse scattering, we show that the polar skyrmion bubbles form a three-dimensional lattice gas: they occupy discrete sites, but their order extends over only a few neighbours and is two to three times stronger across the SrTiO3 spacers than within a layer. This interlayer coupling is consistent with the polarization of the bubbles extending into the spacers. Within each bubble, the polarization rotates in a predominantly Néel-type manner, and Pb and Ti rotate together with comparable picometre displacements, demonstrating that both A- and B-site cations take part in the polar distortion.

title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
abstract: Significant efforts are currently being directed toward the implementation of large-scale quantum information processors, but realizing useful quantum advantage also requires the development of efficient quantum algorithms. While for many practical problems the dominant resource costs are associated with a small set of computational primitives, optimizing them in the quantum setting presents unique challenges, including a reversibility constraint absent from ordinary classical computation. Here we introduce an evolutionary framework in which large language models (LLMs) propose circuit designs and an independent evaluator verifies and scores them. We apply this framework to tasks spanning numerical computation, chemistry, optimization, quantum simulation, and number theory. In seven of the eight tasks, the discovered circuits significantly reduce both Toffoli and qubit counts relative to the state of the art. In the eighth, the search discovers a new reversible architecture for prime-field modular inversion. By handling reversibility differently, the architecture makes divsteps -- a classical algorithm previously impractical for reversible integer arithmetic -- viable and substantially improves the Toffoli-qubit trade-off for modular inversion. These results open the door for evaluator-guided LLM co-design of new algorithmic structures for quantum computation.

title: Subpocket-Aware Fragment-Based Docking Pipeline for Kinase Ligand Design: Methodology and a PKA Case Study
abstract: Protein kinases regulate signal transduction through phosphorylation, and their dysregulation drives diseases like cancer, autoimmune disorders, and Alzheimer’s, making them key drug targets. Fragment-based drug design offers a powerful route to kinase inhibitors but often neglects kinase-specific structural insights. While KinFragLib, a library consisting of 7486 fragments derived from kinase-ligand complexes, provides a rich resource, exhaustive recombination of its fragments is computationally demanding. Here, we present an efficient exploration strategy that integrates subpocket-guided fragment growing with template docking to navigate this vast chemical space. Our automated pipeline prioritizes kinase-specific structural information, enabling targeted generation of chemically diverse ligands. Applied to the PKA kinase, the approach produced 33758 candidate molecules with promising docking scores, of which 15 were synthesized. Seven molecules reduced kinase activity by more than 50% at an inhibitor concentration of 100 μM, and five of these compounds also showed promising efficacy at a concentration of 10 μM. The IC50 determination ultimately revealed that five of the molecules were effective in the two- to three-digit nanomolar range. Crystallographic validation confirmed the predicted binding mode of the most potent compound. This methodology demonstrates how structure-informed guidance can transform fragment-based design into a scalable route for discovering novel kinase inhibitors.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Chiral Phosphoric Acid-Catalyzed Asymmetric Allylic Dearomatization of Tryptamines with Alkoxyallenes
abstract: Catalytic asymmetric dearomatization of tryptamines has emerged as a powerful strategy for constructing chiral pyrroloindoline frameworks, which are ubiquitous in bioactive natural products. Despite tremendous advances in transition-metal-catalyzed synthesis of allyl-substituted pyrroloindolines, organocatalytic approaches remain elusive. Herein, we report a chiral phosphoric acid-catalyzed asymmetric allylic dearomatization of tryptamines with alkoxyallenes.

title: Inverse Design of Optical Metamaterials Assembled from Plasmonic Nanoparticles
abstract: Self-assembly of strongly coupled plasmonic nanoparticles is a scalable and promising route for producing optical metamaterials with emergent photonic properties. Understanding, controlling, and designing the light-matter interactions of these components is crucial to improving their performance. In this paper, we formulate optical metamaterials design as an inverse problem, where we first specify a target optical behavior and then use numerical optimization to autonomously discover self-assembled nanoparticle metamaterials possessing the desired features.

title: Transition state to minimum conversion in the Cope rearrangement under gigapascal pressure
abstract: Converting a transition state (TS) into a minimum is a challenging, yet possible, task, commonly achievable via chemical substitution. Pressure is expected to favor TSs that correspond to volume minima, yet experimentally or computationally demonstrated TS-to-minimum conversions remain rare. Here, we demonstrate a pressure-induced TS-to-minimum conversion in the Cope rearrangement at ∼18 GPa. Extreme pressure polarizable continuum model (XP-PCM) optimizations and vibrational analyses reveal the gradual conversion of the TS imaginary mode into a real vibrational mode.

title: Investigation of NaxFePO4 systems prepared by a modified Pechini sol-gel method as possible cathode materials for high voltage Na-ion batteries
abstract: An uncomplicated modification of a Pechini assisted sol-gel process in water-polyol solutions is proposed for the synthesis of Na-Fe phosphate powders with different Na-ion content as cathode materials for sodium ion batteries (SIBs). Depending on the pH-values, X-ray diffraction detected the formation of Na-poor olivine-like o-NaFePO4 orthorhombic phase and o-FePO4 nanocrystalline structure. The cyclic voltammetry of the SIBs shows reduction peaks at ~2.23 V (x = 1.0) and ~2.12 V (x = 1.2) vs. Na/Na+ for pH < 3, and between 2.8 V - ~3.0 V (x = 1.0) for pH = 5 respectively.

title: One-step synthesis of α-fluoroarylacetic acids from trifluoromethyl arenes via photocatalytic reduction
abstract: A photocatalytic reduction strategy for the direct synthesis of α-fluoroarylacetic acids from readily available trifluoromethyl arenes has been developed. In contrast to conventional approaches, this reaction does not generate undesired oxidation byproducts associated with the use of fluorinating reagents. Investigation of the substrate scope revealed that the reaction tolerates a wide range of functional groups, including dimethylamino, alkynyl, alkenyl, and ether functionalities. Trifluoromethyl-substituted pyridine derivatives were also compatible with the reaction conditions.

title: Graph Theory-Based De Novo Strategy for Automated Generation of Organic Molecular Cage
abstract: The current design and construction of organic molecular cages (OMCs) remain largely constrained by established topological library. To address this challenge, we established a de novo, graph-theory-based strategy that enables the automated generation of OMCs architectures, which require only the chemical structures of building blocks. By decomposing OMCs into distinct topological geometric elements, a system of equations can be established using graph theory to describe the mathematical relationships and geometric constraints for their architectures.

title: Quantum-Entangled Four-Proton Waltz of Anomalous Transport in Water Hydrogen Bond Network
abstract: Proton transfer mechanism along water hydrogen bond network lies in the fundamental question in chemical dynamics. The mechanism remains challenge due to nuclear quantization and many-body correlation. We develop a quantum dynamical model framework that treats electrons and multiple transferring protons on equal footing, and integrate it with isotope measurement by scanning tunneling microscopy of a surface‑bound water tetramer.

title: Enantioselective [3+3] Formal Annulation of Anilines via Carbene Catalysis
abstract: An efficient preparation of highly enantioenriched cyclic compounds from readily available synthons via stereocontrolled organocatalytic processes remains a significant challenge in modern synthetic chemistry. Herein, we report a highly stereoselective N -heterocyclic carbene (NHC)-catalyzed [3+3] annulation of anilines using α-bromocinnamic aldehydes as convenient acyl-azolium precursors. This protocol offers a straightforward route to valuable chiral lactams in high yields (up to 98%) and excellent enantioselectivities (up to 97:3 er ), featuring broad functional group tolerance.

title: Robust and Reusable Waveguide-Enhanced Raman-on-a-Chip for Sensing Complex Fluids
abstract: Integrated photonic sensors offer a pathway toward compact chemical analysis, but their use in unprocessed complex fluids is limited by surface fouling, chemical compatibility, and the need for stable optical coupling. Here, we develop a reusable waveguide-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (WERS) platform based on chemically resilient silicon nitride waveguides and a permanently packaged fiber-to-chip interface. The sensor incorporates a spiral sensing waveguide and a robust optical input/output architecture designed to provide reproducible coupling without active alignment.

title: De Novo Circularly Polarized Emission and Greatly Enhanced Circular Dichroism in Cationic Naphthalene Diimide Dye Supramolecular Assembly on 2-D Laponite Nanoclay
abstract: This study reveals a surprising finding that a chiral cationic pyrrolidine-substituted naphthalene diimide (cNDI-Py + ), which shows no circular dichroism (CD) or circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) in its monomeric form, exhibits strong CD and broad, intense CPL when electrostatically bound to a 2D synthetic laponite nanoclay nanoplatelet (cNDI-Py + _Laponite) in an aqueous environment.

title: Stable triorganoiodine complexes
abstract: The first examples of air stable acyclic triorganoiodine compounds, phenyliodine bis(1-(2-R)-o-carborane)s have been isolated from reactions of PhIL2 reagents with lithio-o-carboranes and crystallographically characterized. When R = H or Si(CH3)3, the complexes are predisposed to form o-carboryne through β-elimination as confirmed by a trapping reaction with naphthalene, where the R = H variant degrades during formation. The latter Si(CH3)3 derivative is isolable in modest yield, while for R = CH3, the resulting phenyliodine bis(1-(2-methyl)-o-carborane)s can be obtained in high yields.

title: Predicting Glass Transition Temperature of Polyimide Homopolymers and Copolymers Using Interpretable QSPR-Based Machine Learning: The MFKit Framework
abstract: In this work, we address the problem of predicting the glass transition temperature of polyimides, a class of high-performance engineering thermoplastics, with an emphasis on both homopolymer and copolymer systems. While machine learning approaches have been widely applied to polymer property prediction, their extension to copolymers remains limited and often lacks the interpretability required for rational materials design.

title: Terminal Acceptor-Substitution Controls Optoelectronic Properties in Triphenylamine Based Donors for Organic Solar Cells: A DFT Approach
abstract: Organic solar cells offer opportunities for lightweight and flexible solar energy conversion, motivating development of molecular systems with tunable optoelectronic properties. In this study, six novel triphenylamine-based small-molecule donors (RD1-RD6) having donor-πacceptor (D-π-A) design, where dimethoxy triphenylamine-donor, thiophene-bridge, and phenyl with 1,3-indandione derivatives-acceptors are investigated to understand how the terminal acceptor regulates their molecular, electronic and excited state properties.

title: De novo design of photoenzymes with substrate-recognition-encoded enantioselectivity
abstract: Photoenzymes enable stereoselective excited-state transformations beyond the chemical space accessible to natural enzymes, yet their development remains largely dependent on repurposing few privileged protein scaffolds and extensive directed evolution. Although de novo protein design enables tailor-made catalytic architectures, its prevailing transition-state stabilization paradigm is not readily transferable to photoenzymes.

title: Synthesis of Amphiphilic Polymer Co-Networks via the Growth of a Living RAFT Network. Part III: Effect of DMSO Content
abstract: Owing to their distinctive nanophase-separated, co-continuous morphology, Amphiphilic polymer co-networks (APCNs) have attracted considerable attention in the past four decades. In 2024, a RAFT-mediated network growth strategy for the synthesis of APCNs was reported. This approach involves first preparing a parent RAFT network, typically a hydrophilic network containing dormant network-RAFT agents, followed by the diffusion and polymerization of hydrophobic monomers within the parent network.

title: Scalable Synthesis and Processing of Porous Organic Polymers for Continuous-Flow Noble Metal Recycling and Catalysis
abstract: Porous organic polymers (POPs) hold great promise for separations and catalysis but remain limited by costly syntheses and poor processability. Here we report the scalable synthesis of freestanding imine/aminal-linked POP gels from inexpensive monomers under mild conditions. The gels can be molded into diverse architectures and converted into mechanically robust monoliths with high surface areas of up to 1055 m2/g. The POPs exhibit high adsorption capacities of 3225 mg/g for [AuCl4]- and 1375 mg/g for [PdCl4]2-.

title: Fe-dopant site occupancy in Co3O4: evidence of isovalent substitution and short-range association at octahedral sites
abstract: Understanding how dopant site occupancy influences the behavior of spinel oxides is essential for tailoring their functional properties. Here, we combine DFT+U calculations with computational and experimental Co K-edge XANES spectroscopy to investigate the structural, electronic, and magnetic effects of Fe incorporation into Co3O4. The results indicate a strong energetic preference for isovalent substitution, with Fe3+ preferentially occupying octahedral Co3+ sites.

title: Microstructural, Energy-Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy, and Fourier-Transform Infrared Analysis of Inorganic-Platelet Polymer Composites for Sustainable Infrastructure
