abstract: Polymer matrix composites used in wet or thermally variable environments may change through moisture diffusion, polymer relaxation, swelling and plasticization, hydrolysis or leaching, microcracking, and progressive weakening of the reinforcement–matrix interface. This paper focuses on understanding the composition and morphology of a reinforcing phase, and determining whether its incorporation produces additional bulk-resolvable chemical features, which is important for interpreting composites used in wet or aggressive environments.

title: Heteroatom Engineering Enables Oxygen-Tolerant Electrochemical Direct Air Capture
abstract: Electrochemical direct CO2 capture using redox-active carriers offers an alternative to thermal amine scrubbing but requires molecules that combine strong CO2 binding with tolerance toward oxygen and water. Here, we show that incorporating pyridinic nitrogen into an ortho-quinone framework provides this combination in 1,10phenanthroline-5,6-dione (PD). Comparison of PD with phenanthrenequinone (PQ) and the analogue 1,10phenanthroline (PT) isolates the role of pyridinic nitrogen in tuning the redox potential and CO2 capture behaviour of the quinone core.

title: Aryne-Enabled Synthesis of 1,8-Disubstituted Thioxanthones for Conformationally Gated Metal-Ion Sensing
abstract: Conformational changes in a chromophore can strongly influence its fluorescence properties. Here, we report the development of thioxanthone-based fluorescent sensors designed to suppress the characteristic butterfly-like deformation of the thioxanthone core upon metal-ion binding. To access the required 1,8-disubstituted scaffolds, we developed an efficient aryne-based synthesis of multisubstituted thioxanthones from readily available o -iodoaryl triflates and N , N , N’ , N’- tetramethylthiourea.

title: Volatile-element depletion in rocky planets as a purity spectrum of a single information field: An information-dynamics reinterpretation of hybrid accretion
abstract: Wang et al. (2026, Nature Astronomy) showed that the moderately-volatile lithophile element (MVLE) depletion patterns of Earth and Mars record different formation pathways: Earth accreted ≳75% of its mass via pebble accretion, Mars ∼73% via collisions of volatile-depleted planetesimals. We reinterpret this result in the information-dynamics (ID) framework, in which self-organization (ε) and dissipation (γ) compete through a single information field of local purity p.

title: Atomic-level visualization of local tacticity and steric structures of polymer chains
abstract: Since Staudinger's demonstration of the macromolecular concept a century ago, polymer science has been built upon the fundamental concept of chain configuration and conformation, which primarily determine polymer properties at both molecular and macroscopic levels. However, direct atomic-level visualization of individual polymer chains has remained a challenge, leaving the fundamental question of how local chain configuration/conformation are involved in the preferred overall chain morphology experimentally unexplored.

title: A Broadly Deployable Method for Repeated Hyperpolarized 13 C Metabolic Imaging in Living Animals
abstract: Hyperpolarized 13 C-MRI enables real-time imaging of metabolic conversions in vivo, but remains largely restricted to specialized sites with superconducting high-field MRI and polarization infrastructure. Here we present a broadly deployable method for preclinical hyperpolarized 13 C-metabolic imaging, which combines signal amplification by reversible exchange (SABRE), a parahydrogen-based hyperpolarization technique, with detection of [1- 13 C]pyruvate-d 3 in a compact 436 mT permanent-magnet small-animal MRI system.

title: Dry-drawn Bi2Te3-on-paper thermoresistive devices for respiration monitoring
abstract: Dry deposition on paper offers a simple route to resistive sensing devices. Here, micronized Bi2Te3 powder is rubbed onto copier paper through a tape mask, charcoal electrodes are drawn over the deposited layer, and copper leads are attached with conductive silver paste; the active layer requires no solvent, binder, vacuum processing or annealing. X-ray diffraction identifies rhombohedral Bi2Te3 with preferred (00l) orientation, while electron microscopy shows particles and platelets distributed over the fibrous substrate.

title: Direct Photo- and Electrothermally Regenerable Adsorbents for Carbon Dioxide Capture Using Conjugated Metal−Organic Frameworks
abstract: Adsorbent regeneration in carbon dioxide capture systems primarily relies on external temperature and pressure swings, posing critical challenges of intensive energy penalties and low cycling rates. Here we demonstrate a direct photo- and electrothermal swing method for CO 2 capture using two-dimensional conjugated MOF Cu 3 (2,3,6,7,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene) 2 (Cu 3 (HHTP) 2 ) and its derivatives. Cu 3 (HHTP) 2 releases CO 2 captured at room-temperature through photo- or electrothermal effects by directly applying one-sun irradiation or a voltage of 10 V.

title: Hybrid Photoactive Lignin Based Magnetic Nanomaterials for Antimicrobial Application
Nonadiabatic Semiclassical Polariton Dynamics: Excited State Proton Transfer of Aminopropenal
abstract: The interplay between strong light-matter coupling and nonadiabatic molecular dynamics provides a promising route to control chemical reactivity. Here, we develop a framework for simulating polaritonic chemistry with on-the-fly semiclassical nonadiabatic molecular dynamics, employing the linearized semiclassical initial value representation. With this approach, we simulate the nonadiabatic molecular dynamics under strong light-matter coupling, presenting results for excited state proton transfer of aminopropenal.

title: Mayer’s Effective Minimal Localized Molecular Orbitals
abstract: Roughly thirty years ago Mayer presented a theory leading to the concept of an effective minimal atomic basis. A set of a posteriori defined, fragment-localized molecular orbitals (LMOs) was obtained as a byproduct. In this work, a new set of LMOs, termed Mayer’s effective minimal LMOs, is derived from this byproduct; it can be viewed as arising from a compactification of atomic orbitals projected onto the occupied space. The procedure is fully self-contained, requiring no input beyond that of the underlying quantum chemical calculation.

title: Sequential Adaptive Natural Density Partitioning (AdNDP) Systematically Produces Non-N-Representable Densities
abstract: Adaptive natural density partitioning (Ad-NDP) sequentially extracts fragment natural orbitals from the one-electron density matrix. Herein, we show, with an exact and basisindependent argument, that the residual density left behind after two non-orthogonal bonding elements are extracted is not guaranteed to be N-representable. The breakdown has a precise, traceable origin: whenever two sequentially depleted orbitals carry a nonzero overlap, S12 ̸= 0, the second extraction re-subtracts density along a direction the first depletion step has already emptied, driving a diagonal element of the…

title: Self-Sustained Sabatier Reaction via Submerged Photosynthesis
abstract: CO 2 methanation is a promising route for carbon utilization, yet conventional processes remain constrained by their reliance on externally supplied H 2 and specialized catalysts. To overcome these limitations, this study introduces a self-sustained Sabatier reaction based on the submerged photosynthesis of crystallites (SPSC). In this single aqueous system, metallic Fe and Mg powders react with carbonated water to generate H 2 and CH 4 near room temperature without an added methanation catalyst. Light irradiation accelerates the production of both gases.

title: Structure-Based Virtual Screening of Enantia chlorantha Stem Bark Constituents Reveals Candidate Pancreatic Alpha-Amylase Inhibitors
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remains a major global health burden, and inhibition of pancreatic alpha-amylase is an established strategy for limiting postprandial hyperglycaemia. Enantia chlorantha stem bark is widely used in Nigerian ethnomedicine, but its alpha-amylase-inhibitory phytoconstituents have not been characterised at the molecular level. This study applied structure-based computational screening to identify candidate alpha-amylase inhibitors from E.

title: Mechanochemically Accelerated Defluorosilylation of α-Trifluoromethyl Styrenes
abstract: We report a mechanochemical copper-catalyzed defluorosilylation of α-trifluoromethyl styrenes with silylboranes. Mechanical activation dramatically accelerated the C–F bond transformation, reducing the reaction time from 8 h to only 30 min at room temperature while substantially decreasing solvent consumption. The reaction exhibits broad substrate compatibility and scalability, highlighting mechanochemistry as an effective strategy for accelerating selective C–F bond functionalization.

title: Methodology for Fabricating and Testing Carbon Molecular Sieve (CMS) Dense Film Membranes for Reproducible Permeation Experiments
abstract: Carbon molecular sieve (CMS) membranes are promising for demanding gas separations, but their brittleness after pyrolysis makes dense-film permeation testing difficult and often irreproducible. Membranes that appear defect-free after pyrolysis can crack during handling, masking, permeation cell assembly, vacuum evacuation or gas pressurization. This work presents a practical procedure for fabricating and testing CMS dense films prepared from fluorinated polyimide-based CMS membranes.

title: Photocatalytic dehydrogenation enables divergent access to functional polyolefins
abstract: Polyolefins are among the most widely used plastics, yet their chemically inert hydrocarbon backbones severely limit opportunities for chemical modification and value-added reuse. Introducing carbon–carbon double bonds offers a powerful way to transform these otherwise unreactive materials into versatile intermediates for downstream chemistry. Here we report an acceptorless photocatalytic/cobalt-catalyzed dehydrogenation that operates across a broad range of polyethylene- and polypropylene-based materials, including post-consumer plastics.

title: Lithographically Patterned Cobalt Nanoribbons as Magnetic Artificial Pinning Centers in REBCO-Coated Conductors for Continuous-Wave Accelerator Magnets
abstract: We investigate a lithographically patterned cobalt-nanoribbon array as a magnetic artificial pinning center (APC) architecture for REBCO-coated conductors intended for continuous-wave (CW) superconducting accelerator magnets, using accelerator-driven subcritical (ADS) fission-waste-transmutation injectors as the motivating application. A long-wavelength magnetostatic model (the Wallace/Karlqvist spacing-loss approximation used in magnetic-recording physics) is used to estimate the periodic stray-field harmonic produced above the array as a function of the ribbon fill fraction and…

title: Recycling of PFAS using magnesium through mechanochemical process
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widely used a class of organofluorine compounds whose high chemical and thermal stability has motivated the development of strategies for their chemical conversion and fluorine recovery from the perspective of effective fluorine resource utilization. Herein, we report a mechanochemical strategy for the recovery and utilization of fluorine using alkaline-earth metals. Mechanochemical treatment of polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) with Mg rapidly converted the fluoropolymer into MgF2, and the method was extended to various PFAS.

title: Supramolecular Eutectogels Based on Mangiferin, a Glucose-Appended Natural Herbal Compound
abstract: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have attracted considerable attention as sustainable, next-generation solvents. In this study, we report the formation of supramolecular eutectogels using mangiferin (MF), a naturally occurring C -glucosyl xanthone. MF successfully induced gelation in typical DESs composed of choline chloride and various hydrogen-bond donors, including urea, ethylene glycol, and glycerol. The gelation behavior was dependent on the hydrogen-bond donor, with significant differences observed in the time required for gelation.

title: Residue Protonation States Shape the Photodynamics of Red Fluorescent Proteins
abstract: Understanding the protonation equilibria of key residues in fluorescent proteins, particularly those buried and involved in hydrogen bonding with the chromophore, is crucial for modeling their photodynamical behavior. Using mCherry as a model system, we investigate the protonation effects of two ionizable residues, GLU 215 and LYS 70, located within 4 Å of the chromophore, on the protein's photodynamics.

title: Off-the-Shelf ReaxFF Parameter Sets Underestimate O–O Bond Strengths in Organic Peroxides: A Static and Kinetic Benchmark for Thermal-Hazard Assessment
abstract: ReaxFF reactive molecular dynamics (MD) is increasingly used to study organic peroxide decomposition, although the parameter sets supplied with common MD codes were developed for other chemistries. We benchmarked the six C/H/O ReaxFF parameter sets distributed with LAMMPS against CBS-APNO O–O bond dissociation enthalpies (BDEs) of 13 peroxides and tested whether the static error carries over to the kinetics. All six sets underestimate the O–O BDE (mean signed errors of −11.9 to −30.5 kcal mol-1) and correlate only weakly with the references (r = 0.14–0.50).

title: Imaging of ultrafast electronic and chemical dynamics in biological systems
abstract: Ultrafast electron microscopy (UEM) has enabled real-space visualization of dynamics in inorganic nanomaterials on fundamental timescales, but its application to functional biological nanostructures remains largely unexplored. Here, we use time-resolved UEM and electron energyloss spectroscopy (EELS) to probe the photoinduced electronic response and the light-induced chemical modification of the conductive periplasmic nanofiber network extracted from filamentous cable bacteria.

title: Harvesting photosynthetic reducing power stored
Electrochemical Reduction of Acetonitrile to Gaseous C2 Products and Implications for Small Molecule Transformations
abstract: Acetonitrile (CH3CN) is a polar aprotic solvent that is widely used in electrochemistry due to its large dielectric constant, strong ability to solubilize numerous substrates and catalysts, and stability under a wide range of applied potentials. In the context of electrocatalysis, reaction rates and product selectivities can differ markedly in CH3CN relative to other solvents, but the possibility of solvent reduction remains poorly explored. Herein, we report that CH3CN is reduced electrochemically in the presence of organic acids to form ethylene, ethane, ethylamine and ammonia.

title: Vertical ionization energies from inverse generalized Kohn-Sham calculations at fixed electron density
abstract: The exact Kohn--Sham (KS) system must have its highest occupied orbital energy equal to the negative of the lowest vertical ionization energy (VIE). No comparable theorem connects the deeper occupied levels $\varepsilon_k$ to the higher VIEs $I_k$. Chong, Gritsenko and Baerends (CGB) established empirically that $I_k + \varepsilon_k\propto\sqrt{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{HOMO}}-\varepsilon_k}$. We ask whether a similar relation holds for the exact generalized Kohn-Sham (GKS) system, which incorporates a fraction $α$ of Hartree-Fock exchange. We invert near-exact CCSD/aug-cc-pVQZ ground-state densities of LiH, LiF, H$_2$O, HF, CO, N$_2$ and F$_2$ at $α= 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0$ and obtain the exact GKS systems at each admixture. As the density is held fixed and only the operator is varied, the resulting occupied spectra separate the effect of exact-exchange admixture on orbital energies from its effect on the density, two contributions inseparable in a self-consistent hybrid calculation. The CGB relation holds broadly across the family, with a proportionality coefficient linear in $α$, $c(α)=c(0)-sα$, where $c(0)=1.185\pm0.017$ eV$^{1/2}$ and $s=1.987\pm0.041$ eV$^{1/2}$, with $R^{2}\ge0.9996$ for H$_2$O, CO, HF and N$_2$. Using the response-potential matrix elements tabulated by Gritsenko, Braïda and Baerends, we decompose the CGB coefficient into response and spectroscopic parts, and find $s$ to agree with the homogeneous-electron-gas step-height coefficient $K_g = 1.9932$ eV$^{1/2}$, which we conjecture is its origin. The coefficient vanishes at $α^{*}=0.597\pm0.008$. At $α^{*}$ the HOMO-referenced GKS occupied levels satisfy $\varepsilon_k\approx-I_k$ across the whole occupied range. The zero crossing is fixed by the core orbitals; in the outer valence the CGB coefficient is already indistinguishable from zero at $α=0$.

title: Not All Unlabeled Data Are Equal: Unlabeled Data Selection for Semi-Supervised QSAR Modeling with Large Chemical Repositories
abstract: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) is particularly attractive in domains where labels are expensive to obtain, while unlabeled examples are readily available. Quantitative Structure-Activity Relationship (QSAR) modeling, which predicts molecular biological activity from chemical structure, is one such domain. Obtaining activity measurements requires costly wet-lab experiments, resulting in small labeled datasets, while chemical repositories such as ChEMBL contain millions of unlabeled molecules. Despite this apparent suitability, the potential of large chemical databases to improve QSAR models via SSL remains largely unexplored. Furthermore, it is unclear how unlabeled data should be selected in realistic SSL settings with genuine unlabeled data. We conduct a systematic study of unlabeled-data selection using 10 QSAR datasets extracted from ChEMBL and a pool of more than 400,000 unlabeled molecules. To this end, we evaluate three established SSL algorithms (self-training, co-training, and label propagation) and formulate four unlabeled-data selection strategies based on random, nearest-neighbor, furthest-neighbor, and mixed sampling. Our results show that unlabeled data from large chemical repositories can improve QSAR models, with at least one SSL configuration outperforming the supervised baseline on each of the 10 datasets. Moreover, the most reliable improvements are generally achieved by selecting a relatively small number of chemically distant molecules. This suggests that the composition of the unlabeled set may be more important than its size, challenging the common premise that SSL necessitates an abundance of unlabeled data.

title: Coherent and Incoherent Time-Resolved Diffuse Scattering Intensity from First Principles
abstract: Time-resolved diffuse scattering from X-ray free-electron lasers and ultrafast electron diffraction gives access to the nonequilibrium lattice dynamics of photoexcited solids in reciprocal space. Existing interpretations have often relied on simplified models. Here we present a first-principles formulation of the time-dependent first-order diffuse intensity in which coherent and incoherent contributions emerge on equal footing. By assuming the probe-pulse coherence time to be longer than the characteristic electronic timescales, but shorter than those of the ionic motion, we work in the density-matrix formalism and derive equations of motion for the displacement-displacement correlators in a basis of instantaneous, out-of-equilibrium Born-Oppenheimer normal modes. We show how the incoherent contribution, governed by the phonon occupations, and a coherent contribution, governed by the anomalous phonon correlators, emerge. The non-trivial coherent dynamics is shown to be induced both by the photoinduced phonon-frequency shift and by electron-phonon scattering off the nonequilibrium carrier distribution. We implement the resulting equations using Wannier interpolation in the \textsc{EPI}q code and apply them to photoexcited germanium. The calculated diffuse intensity reproduces both the oscillation frequencies and the rising incoherent background observed experimentally, opening the way to a systematic interpretation of time-resolved diffuse scattering in ultrafast experiments.

title: A Comparative Benchmark of GAN, DDPM, and Flow Matching for 2D and 3D Porous Microstructures Synthesis
abstract: Accurate representations of porous microstructures are essential for studying transport and effective properties in geomaterials such as clay, carbonate, and sandstone. Deep generative models provide a means of producing additional statistically representative microstructures, but different model families can differ substantially in their ability to reproduce morphology, population variability, and transport-relevant connectivity.

title: Interfacial Assembly of 2D Superlattices and Quasicrystals in Binary Nanoparticle Systems with Strong Unlike Interactions
abstract: Two-dimensional nanoparticle (NP) superlattices assembled at fluid–fluid interfaces offer a versatile platform for creating novel materials with applications in plasmonics, spectroscopy, photonics, and catalysis. Recently, we implemented a basin-hopping Monte Carlo approach to identify ground-state configurations of binary NP assemblies at fluid interfaces, which helped predict a range of ordered superlattices, several of which have been observed experimentally.

title: Synthesis of Amphiphilic Polymer Co-Networks via the Growth of a Living RAFT Network. Part II: PEGDA-Based Parent Networks
abstract: This work represents the second part of our series on the synthesis of amphiphilic polymer co-networks (APCNs) via the growth of a living RAFT (reversible additionfragmentation chain transfer) network. In this work, we explore the photogrowth behavior of crosslinked polyethylene glycol diacrylate 700 (PEGDA 700) as a hydrophilic parent RAFT network. The model hydrophobic monomers—butyl acrylate (BuA) and methyl methacrylate (MMA)—were incorporated into the parent network via photogrowth, ultimately forming APCNs.

title: A General Suzuki–Miyaura/[2+2] Photocycloaddition Approach to 2-Oxabicyclo[2.1.1]hexane Biaryl Mimetics
abstract: Herein, we report a modular approach to monosubstituted, (hetero)arylated 2-oxabicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (oxa-BCHs). The strategy combines facile Suzuki–Miyaura cross-couplings to assemble suitable diene precursors that can undergo [2+2] photocycloadditions. Nineteen novel (hetero)aromatic building blocks and fragments are constructed from their respective (hetero)aryl boronates, conveniently accessed from commercial sources.

title: Synthesis and characterization of polyazomethines – Towards a semiconducting paper
abstract: Novel organic semiconductor poly(azomethine) materials were synthesized via the polycondensation of terephthalaldehyde with two distinct diamines: para-phenylenediamine and 4,4’-diaminodiphenylmethane. These synthetic routes yielded a fully conjugated polyimine (P1) and a polyimine featuring a more restricted conjugation domain interrupted by a methylene spacer (P2), respectively. A comparative study was conducted to evaluate the influence of the conjugation length on some of their properties, mainly optoelectrical.

title: The Role of Metacognitive Skills in Decision-Making using Type I/II Thinking
abstract: Strong reasoning skills are vital in a variety of academic and everyday contexts, requiring strong metacognitive awareness to be strategic and efficient. However, relatively little is known about how metacognitive abilities and skill-building relate to making purposeful choices about reasoning. We investigated the role of metacognition in Dual Process theory, including learners’ awareness and self-description of their cognitive engagement.

title: Natural abundance isotopomics reveals coordinated amino acid metabolic alterations in human lung cancer
abstract: Background Metabolic reprogramming in cancer is usually characterized through changes in metabolite levels, yet pool size alone does not reveal how elements are routed through tumour metabolism. We investigated whether natural abundance isotopomics could resolve this metabolic organization in human lung cancer from bulk tissue to individual protein-bound amino acids.

title: From Cancer to Infection: An amphiphilic ABAC Phthalocyanine for Versatile Phototherapy
abstract: The development of photosensitizers capable of operating across multiple therapeutic photoprocesses remains a major challenge in photomedicine. Herein, we report a cationic amphiphilic ABAC zinc(II) phthalocyanine (ZnPc-Me) obtained by a direct [3+1] mixed cyclization strategy followed by post-functional quaternization/transalkylation. The controlled amphiphilic architecture promotes optimal membrane anchoring while suppressing aggregation in lipid environments.

title: Divergent Two-Carbon Insertion of Alcohols
abstract: Carbon-chain extension enables systematic modification of molecular frameworks, yet general two-carbon homologation of alcohols remains underdeveloped. Herein, we report a divergent two-carbon extension of primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols through a radical–polar relay. Photocatalytic radical C–O bond cleavage merged with vinylsulfonium salt enabled a subsequent nucleophilic substitution to afford divergent two-carbon insertion products with oxygen-, nitrogen-, sulfur-, and carbon-based nucleophiles.

title: Directing group-free site-selective and stereoretentive C-H amination of alkanes with phenyl triazolinedione (PTAD) as a σ-acid
abstract: 4-Phenyl-1,2,4-triazoline-3,5-dione (PTAD) is known as the most reactive commercially available dienophile, as it rapidly reacts with dienes at low temperatures and high dilution. In general terms, PTAD is a very soft Lewis acid, with a strong affinity towards electron rich alkenes. In this work, we report that the potent π-acid PTAD also shows a very useful and general σ-acid reactivity towards electron rich C(sp3)-H bonds, opening up its use in alkane amination reactions, as well as in late stage functionalization applications.

title: Stereospecific Conversion of Alkenyl and Epoxy Carbamates into Cyclic Carbonate Alcohols
abstract: We have thoroughly explored the conversion of alkenyl and epoxy carbamates into cyclic carbonate alcohols. The substrate scope is robust, and the products are amenable to further transformations. In almost all cases, the reactions are predictably regioselective and stereospecific. The reactions can be run open to air and without precautions to exclude moisture. Indeed, H2O plays a critical role in the transformations and is added to the reactions as a key reagent.

title: Immunodetection of a Cell-Surface Biomarker via the Freezing of Supercooled Water Droplets
abstract: Immunolabels traditionally detect biomarkers via a color change or fluorescence. The frequently weak signals from low biomarker concentrations prompted the development of numerous enzymatic amplification strategies. Although very effective for signal generation, these strategies increase the complexity, cost, and time required for immunoassays. What if water itself could generate and self-amplify a signal to detect a biomarker? Here, we demonstrate that it is possible to detect a cell-surface protein biomarker by inducing the phase change from water to ice in supercooled water droplets.

title: Towards decoding the structure of the water-magnetite interface
abstract: HypothesisThe molecular structure of water at iron-oxide interfaces is determined by the protonation state, orientation and population of interfacial OH species. These microscopic features can be decoded by combining surface-specific vibrational spectroscopy with reactive and accurate molecular dynamics simulations. In this way, it could be possible to connect the measured nonlinear optical response to specific molecular configurations at the magnetite-water interface, resolving the interfacial water structure. Experiments and simulationsWe investigated magnetite films in contact with liquid water at neutral and alkaline pH using phase-resolved sum-frequency generation (SFG) spectroscopy in the OH/OD stretching region and Fresnel correction of the optical response. In parallel, neural-network-potential molecular dynamics simulations were used to model the water-magnetite interface and identify interfacial water species, quantify their orientations, hydrogen-bonding environments and lifetimes, and compute species resolved SFG spectra. FindingsThe combined analysis assigns distinct spectral features to dissociated surface OH groups, hydroxyls and water molecules adsorbed on octahedral iron sites, water bound at dissociation sites and water molecules above tetrahedral rows. The simulations reveal a reactive interfacial hydroxyl network with nanosecond-scale rearrangements and strong species-dependent hydrogen bonding. Experimentally, the SFG spectra show pronounced pH dependence, consistent with changes in surface charge and hydroxylation. A systematic difference between measured and computed SFG spectra indicates that the assumed surface model of magnetite does not fully represent the aqueous interface. This discrepancy provides a molecular constraint for improved models of magnetite-water interfaces and highlights SFG spectroscopy/ML-MD comparison as a valuable route to resolving oxide-water interfacial structures.
venue: Journal of colloid and interface science

title: Putting a Temperature on Electron Correlation
abstract: It is common wisdom that a better understanding of how to quantify electron correlation should lead to more efficient treatments of the correlation problem. Here, we not only substantiate this view but turn it into a concrete, systematic framework for ground states. Since prominent correlation measures such as the nonfreeness depend only on the one-particle reduced density matrix, modeling the correlation energy as a function of such a measure naturally places the framework within reduced density matrix functional theory, while keeping the cost at mean-field level. Strikingly, the variable conjugate to the measure emerges as a ``correlation temperature'', thereby connecting correlation measures, functional theory, and effective temperatures. The framework rationalizes methods such as i-DMFT, and we illustrate its key concepts analytically for the Hubbard dimer and numerically for small molecular systems. This brings a fundamental question within reach: how much of the correlation problem can be solved at mean-field cost?

title: DropKV: Decoupling Residual-Output Perturbation for Near-Optimal KV-Cache Eviction
abstract: Key-value (KV) cache management has become a critical bottleneck for scaling Large Language Models (LLMs) to long-context scenarios due to linear memory growth. While recent eviction methods have moved beyond simple attention-score heuristics to incorporate value representations, they typically face a fundamental trade-off: the underlying optimization for minimizing output perturbation is an NP-hard combinatorial problem, leading to mathematically suboptimal heuristics or implementations that are difficult to kernelize. In this work, we propose DropKV, a simple principled eviction framework based on Decoupled Residual-Output Perturbation. By decoupling the joint eviction decision into independent per-token scoring, DropKV circumvents combinatorial intractability and admits a provable constant-factor approximation guarantee under a cone condition that we empirically verify on three long-context LLMs. To ensure practical viability, we provide a high-performance implementation using fused Triton kernels that avoid materializing the full attention matrix, delivering a 19.8x scoring-kernel speedup that translates to up to a 9.9% matched-batch end-to-end prefill speedup. Extensive evaluations on the RULER and LongBench benchmarks demonstrate that DropKV consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines at equivalent cache budgets, achieving the lowest inference latency among eviction methods while also remaining faster than the dynamic cache baseline.

title: Rovibrational cross sections for the CO$_2$ $00^00$, $01^10$, $02^20$ and Fermi resonance states $10^00(1)$ and $10^00(2)$ in collisions with He atoms
abstract: We present quantum scattering calculations of CO$_2$-He state-to-state integral cross sections for 25 transition sets, covering pure rotational transitions within and rovibrational transitions between: the ground state $00^00$, the bend fundamental $01^10$, the bending overtone $02^20$, and the Fermi doublet states $10^00(1)$ and $10^00(2)$. Exact coupled-channel (CC) and coupled-states approximation (CSA) calculations are performed using a new five-dimensional potential energy surface. The calculations cover collision energies from 20 to 5220 cm$^{-1}$, sufficient to obtain converged rate coefficients over 100-800 K, and include initial rotational states for each transition up to at least $j=35$. We present an energy-grid algorithm for rovibrational quantum scattering calculations that minimizes the number of separate calculations required. The resulting cross sections exhibit a dominant $Δj=0$ propensity and parity-dependent patterns. For the benchmark $00^00,j' \leftarrow 01^10,j$ transition, thermally averaged rate coefficients reproduce available experimental data. A comparison between the CC and CSA cross sections shows that, for vibrational quenching transitions, the CSA cross sections increasingly deviate from the CC results with increasing initial rotational state $j$. Calculated integral cross sections cover collision energies and rotational states needed to derive rate coefficients for non local thermal equilibrium radiative transfer modeling of mid-infrared CO$_2$ spectra. The computationally simpler CO$_2$-He system allows the methodology and approximations to be tested at high collision energies and rotational states, helping assess their suitability for the more complex and astrochemically important CO$_2$-H$_2$ system.
authors: Floris F. S. van der Tak

title: Beyond Fixed Acquisition Functions: Temporal Difference Active Learning for Perturbation Discovery
abstract: Genetic and drug perturbation screens are important tools for elucidating disease mechanisms and validating therapeutic targets, but experimental costs limit the number of candidates that can be tested. Existing perturbation screening methods typically update the surrogate model with feedback while keeping the acquisition function fixed, limiting their ability to adapt selection to different response landscapes. Experimental feedback reveals current hits and informs subsequent selection by updating candidate predictions, providing a training signal for learning how to select experiments. We formulate budgeted perturbation discovery as a sequential decision problem and propose Temporal Difference Active Learning (TDAL), which learns an acquisition function online through temporal difference learning from a single screening trajectory, accounting for current hits and future discoveries. TDAL uses the Hellinger distance between hit probabilities for unmeasured candidates before and after an experiment to weight successor value, and reuses measured outcomes through leave-batch-out (LBO) to construct virtual transitions and alleviate training data scarcity. Across eight public screens spanning single, double, and triple perturbations under varied experimental configurations, TDAL achieves an average rank of 1.63 among eleven methods and ranks first on four tasks, demonstrating its adaptability across response landscapes.

title: Simulated Solvation Dynamics of a Photoexcited Organic Molecule and the Associated Time-Resolved X-ray Scattering Signal
abstract: Solvation shell reorganization is a key component of the dynamics after photoexcitation of a solvated molecule, especially for charge-transfer excitation in polar solvents. These structural dynamics can be directly observed with time-resolved X-ray solution scattering (TR-XSS) experiments. However, disentangling the scattering signal of solvation-shell reorganization can be challenging, especially for systems containing only light atoms. Here, nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations of a hemithioindigo chromophore in acetonitrile are used to investigate the solvation dynamics upon photoinduced charge transfer as well as vibrational excitation and cooling, and to characterize the corresponding time-resolved X-ray scattering signals. It is found that charge transfer induces rapid reorientation of the first solvation shell (0.15-0.2 ps) followed by slower reorientational and solvent redistribution within and between shells (1-2 ps). An analysis of the volume around the solute excluded to the solvent reveals an initial contraction of the solvation shell, followed by transient rebound within the first 0.4 ps, and then slower contraction. Instantaneous vibrational excitation expands the excluded volume, reaching a maximum near 0.4 ps, followed by contraction during cooling with biexponential relaxation. Low-q features in both the calculated solute-solvent and solvent-solvent scattering signals reflect rearrangements within the first solvation shell and redistribution across shells, while higher-q solute-solvent features more closely follow local first-shell restructuring. These results show that TR-XSS can provide information on both local solvent rearrangements and redistribution across solvation shells and demonstrate that interpreting the scattering signals requires accounting for changes in solvent packing induced by vibrational heating and cooling of the solute.

title: Multi-sourced AI Tutor for Non-Native English Speaker Students
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being adopted as teaching tools in computing education, particularly for developing AI tutors capable of answering student questions. With the rise in enrollment of international students in computing programs, researchers have begun to explore the difficulties that non-native English speaker (NNES) students face in computing courses due to language barriers. To aid such students, we developed a general-purpose AI tutor system that can process student questions in foreign languages (currently focused on Mandarin) and provide bilingual responses. Our system also incorporates the functionality of generating a glossary of technical terms and their explanations to enhance comprehension. Our approach utilizes a specialized Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline with a novel question extraction mechanism, enabling us to effectively utilize a diverse array of course materials for answering student queries. We evaluated our AI tutor using 91 Piazza posts, demonstrating that it could answer 83.52% of the posts correctly and in a helpful manner. The tutor also provided high-quality translations for 76.92% of the questions and generated technical term glossaries for 64.47% of them. Our findings underscore the potential of multi-source RAG pipeline in enhancing AI tutor systems, offering support for non-native speakers that are challenging to provide with traditional supporting staff of a computing course.

title: Low-Energy Vertical Organic Synaptic Transistors Enabled by Siloxane Crosslinking-Induced Edge-On Molecular Ordering
abstract: The von Neumann bottleneck has driven the development of low-power neuromorphic devices such as vertical organic synaptic transistors (VOSTs), which offer ultrashort charge transport pathways and high integration density. However, their performance is still limited by poor molecular ordering and the difficulty in achieving effective gate-controlled modulation.

title: Large Language Model-Assisted Prediction and Virtual Screening of Near-Infrared-II Fluorescent Molecules
abstract: Fluorescence imaging in the second near-infrared window (NIR-II, 1000-1700 nm) has attracted increasing attention in biomedical applications owing to its deep tissue penetration, high spatial resolution, and low background autofluorescence. However, the rational optimization of high-performance NIR-II fluorophores remains challenging because of the complex relationship between molecular structure and optical properties.

title: Hybrid modeling for improved structure prediction of large protein complexes
abstract: An automated framework, HDOCK-Multimer (HDM), is developed that integrates ab initio docking and combinatorial assembly for the structure prediction of large protein complexes. Across three benchmarks, HDM demonstrates increased accuracy and robustness in modeling large protein assemblies, compared with state-of-the-art assembly and deep learning-based methods.

title: Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Response Tensors in Crystalline Magnets: Application to Kagome Metals
abstract: The prediction of response tensors from magnetic textures is a crucial challenge in the study of noncollinear magnets. Existing methods for constructing descriptors of a given response tensor are limited to first-order multipole expansions or restricted to simple magnetic structures. In this work, we construct a complete symmetry-invariant descriptor basis for arbitrary crystal structures and magnetic textures, providing interpretable features for machine learning modeling of response tensors. We modify the standard principal component analysis framework and derive uncorrelated order parameters that are hierarchically stable: extending the order parameter space to include higher-degree spin order introduces additional order parameters that are uncorrelated to the previous ones. We apply this framework to regression and classification of the anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) in a magnetic kagome lattice. In particular, in the regime where AHC is well modeled by linear regression of the symmetry-invariant order parameters, we find that the squared regression coefficients, ranked by their magnitude, obey a Zipf-like power law: $β_{r}^2 \propto r^{-α}$. Our method provides a systematic route to construct interpretable order parameters of all spin orders that connect the symmetry of a magnetic crystal to its response tensors.

title: A Comprehensive Survey of Crystal Structural Prototypes: Construction, Classification, and Applications
abstract: Crystal structural prototypes describe recurring atomic arrangements across chemically distinct materials. Prototype libraries are built through crystallographic curation, standardization, geometric matching, local-environment clustering, and periodic-graph analysis, and support chemical substitution, derivative enumeration, high-throughput screening, structure solution, crystal structure prediction (CSP), and generative design. This survey compares methods by the structural information they retain and the equivalence rules they impose, distinguishing crystallographic structure types, geometric realizations, chemistry-anonymous topologies, and chemical decorations. We review curated and automatically extracted prototype libraries (AFLOW, CSPD, LAE-ICSPD, EMFDTW, TYPIX, ICSD structure types), their source databases, and algorithms for assigning family membership. A GraphID-based analysis of samples from ICSD, the Materials Project, OQMD, and LeMat shows that the 100 most frequent families in each sample cover 30 to 67 percent of analyzed structures, while 72 to 82 percent of observed families are singletons. The GraphIDs of up to 76 percent of structures change when the neighbor tolerance is varied. In our comparison of 12 generative CSP models, template retrieval achieves the highest top-1 success rate. Removing a reduced-stoichiometry class from training introduces new failures in 50 to 78 percent of the test structures of that class, which measures sensitivity to stoichiometric coverage, not generalization to unseen prototypes. We relate these findings to earlier statistics of structure types, space groups, and periodic nets, and to protein-fold coverage studies. We propose independent-database coverage measurements, discovery-rate analyses, and family-held-out tests to assess how prototype reuse affects prediction accuracy, generalization, and novelty.

title: UCEC: A Knowledge Graph-Assisted Machine Learning for Molecular-Mechanism-Interpretable Natural Product-Disease Association Prioritization
abstract: Natural products (NPs) have been considered a critical source of therapeutic drugs, but prioritizing NP-disease associations remain challenging because supporting evidence is distributed across multiple ingredients, targets, protein interactions, and pathways. Herein, we propose a knowledge graph-assisted machine learning model: Uncertainty-Calibrated Evidence-Chains (UCEC) for prioritizing NP-disease associations. UCEC separates predicted association strength from the evidence-conditioned stability of local mechanistic support.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Single-atom-anchored covalent organic frameworks for photocatalytic hydrogen evolution: design principles, dynamic mechanisms, and emerging opportunities
abstract: Photocatalytic water splitting is a promising route for solar-to-hydrogen conversion, but organic photocatalysts are often limited by strong exciton binding, rapid charge recombination, inefficient carrier transport, and sluggish proton-reduction kinetics. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer molecularly tunable structures and electronic properties, yet pristine COFs generally lack efficient catalytic sites. Incorporating single-atom sites (SA sites) into COFs can simultaneously provide active hydrogen-evolution centers and regulate local charge-transfer pathways.

title: Chemically Amplified Photoalignment for Grayscale Programming of Molecular Order and Optical Anisotropy in Liquid Crystal Polymers
abstract: Next-generation optical devices for beam shaping, spatial light modulation, and information storage will benefit from scalable methods to program molecular anisotropy in processable soft materials. Liquid crystal polymers (LCPs) are attractive platforms for this purpose because they combine orientational mobility and long-range order with the processability of polymeric materials, yet a general strategy for high-fidelity grayscale control of molecular order in single-layer LCP films remains an unmet challenge. Here, we address this challenge through molecular design of an azobenzene/cyanobiphenyl side-chain LCP, where a small fraction of photoisomerizable azobenzene units transduces visible light into bulk alignment of a birefringent cyanobiphenyl-rich matrix. This chemically amplified photoalignment strategy preserves light penetration while producing order parameters up to S ≈ 0.58. Excitation intensity controls molecular order through a thresholded and saturating response, captured by an empirical calibration that enables grayscale projections to be translated into spatial maps of molecular alignment along a specific axis. Photomask-free digital projections produced high-fidelity birefringent features down to ∼10 μm and an effective optical bit-depth exceeding 6 bits. Intensity-to-response correction improved grayscale fidelity in complex images and was transferable from microscale to centimeter-scale projection areas. This approach provides a scalable route to programming coupled opacity and polarization-dependent optical behavior in solid LCP films.

title: A light-activated morphine derivative relieves pain in mice
abstract: Local activation could deliver targeted therapy with fewer side effects

title: Network Pharmacology and Bioinformatic Prediction of Five Medicinal-Food Homologous Plants Against the Progression from Chronic Atrophic Gastritis to Gastric Cancer
abstract: Chronic atrophic gastritis (CAG) progresses through distinct pathological stages to gastric cancer. This computational study employed network pharmacology and bioinformatics to predict the active compounds, targets, and pathways of five medicinal-food homologous plants (Houttuyniae Herba, Mume Fructus, Rhizoma Dioscoreae, Portulacae Herba, and Curcumae longae Rhizoma) against this progression. We identified 28 active compounds and 242 targets from TCMSP.
venue: Omics : a journal of integrative biology

title: Comment on "Skyrmion Hall Effect in Altermagnets"
abstract: In their Letter, Jin et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 133, 196701 (2024)] predict a transverse velocity $v_y$ for skyrmions driven by spin-transfer torque (STT), known as skyrmion Hall effect (SkHE), in d-wave altermagnets. Usually, the SkHE emerges from the skyrmion's topological charge which here cancels between sublattices. Instead, Jin et al. attribute the SkHE to the dimensionless quadrupole tensor $A_{ij}$. The result in their Eq. (12) is fitted to micromagnetic simulations, yielding a finite value for $A_{xy}$. However, via the divergence theorem, $A_{ij}$ simplifies to a boundary integral that vanishes for a sufficiently smooth and localized texture. In this Comment, we substantiate our claim from Ref. [2] that the numerically observed SkHE by Jin et al. for a micromagnetic model with standard Zhang-Li STT in the individual sublattices is merely a discretization artefact.

title: Null Controls Are Necessary but Not Sufficient: Evaluating Acceptance Guards for Scientific Discovery and Interpretability
abstract: Automated discovery systems propose scientific explanations and test which to accept. Does passing a test establish the intended claim? We develop four executable operations for changing physical descriptions: identifying redundancies (L1), coarse-graining dynamics (L2), transferring structure (L3), and inferring missing quantities from conservation imbalances (L4). We evaluate these operations and three interpretability settings through null acceptance (NAR), positive acceptance (PAR), and consequence agreement (CAR). A reduction mapping every state to zero predicts its own future perfectly. It passes closure on 96% of 129 public chaotic systems despite retaining no dynamical variation. An independent observable-preservation test rejects it throughout. On controlled benchmarks, the combined criteria accept 24/24 genuine reductions and reject 72/72 nulls. The other operations distinguish symmetries from redundancies, validate transfers, and reject spurious conservation imbalances. In language and ESM-2 protein models, linear CKA remains unchanged when a proposed correspondence is randomly rotated, whereas localized interventions distinguish genuine mappings from tested nulls. In sparse autoencoders, enrichment rejects all 16 tested nulls, yet independent ablation supports 45% of evaluable enriched features, compared with 0.5% of matched controls. These results reveal two acceptance gaps: descriptive tests can accept scientifically empty candidates, and accepted candidates can lack independently verified consequences. Reliable automated discovery requires evaluating both what a test accepts and the scientific consequences it establishes. Code and data: https://real-project-aether.github.io/project-aether/.

title: Investigation of the Performance of Machine Learning Algorithms of Casson-Micropolar Nano Particles Around a Cylindrical Shape: ANN and PINN
abstract: Present study deals with a comprehensive analysis of Micropolar-Casson fluid model in two dimensional through a porous cylinder. In order to represent an accurate complex transport scenario encountered in Industrial and engineering applications formulated mathematical model incorporates Joule heating, heat source, mixed convection, chemical reaction and radiation. Convective boundary conditions were assumed. Non-similar transformations were employed to proposed system of nonlinear equations to get ordinary equations.

title: AI use in STEM PhD dissertations reaches 29%, study finds
abstract: Although artificial intelligence can streamline writing tasks, researchers worry overreliance could impact the development of students’ scientific expertise

title: HumanToxPredict: An interpretable data-driven framework for human oral TDLo prediction and toxicity assessment of pharmaceuticals and bioactive compounds
abstract: Predicting the human toxic dose low (TDLo) is critically important for pharmaceutical safety assessment and regulatory toxicology. A global computational toxicology framework that integrates toxicity data for children, infants, men, and women was developed using indicator-variable-based demographic encoding. Initially, Partial Least Squares (PLS)-based quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) and quantitative read-across structure-activity relationship (q-RASAR) models were developed using interpretable molecular descriptors and similarity-based descriptors.

title: Evolutionary Informed Translation from Protein to Nucleic Acid Sequence
abstract: The choice of nucleic acid sequence for a given protein strongly impacts function and is species-specific. Current protein-to-nucleic-acid translation models treat sequences in isolation, often over-favoring frequently used codons. To generate more natural nucleic acid sequences, we introduce PINATA (Phylogenetically Informed protein to Nucleic Acid Translation with sequence Alignment), a model that leverages sequences from related species encoded in multiple sequence alignments (MSAs) to guide prediction. Our architecture leverages evolutionary context and learns species-and protein specific context to make biologically-informed predictions. Evaluated across 61,934 gene trees and 882 species, PINATA generates sequences that mirror the naturally-occurring sequence substantially better than existing language models. PINATA leverages MSA data to improve exact native codon recovery by 17.95 percentage points over existing language models, effectively preserves natural rare-codon nuances, and more closely matches native sequence properties. PINATA maintains strong predictive performance even with limited evolutionary data. While previous methods largely treated sequences from different species in isolation, our method leverages the evolutionary relationships between nucleic acids and proteins across species to create a more biologically-informed translation. We demonstrate that leveraging rich evolutionary data through an biologically-designed method strongly aids in translating protein sequences to nucleic acid sequences across species. We will make data and code publicly available upon publication.

title: Valley-Selective Transport through Structural Domain Walls in Rhombohedral Graphene Quarter Metals
abstract: Domain walls separating quarter metals with opposite valley polarizations have recently been imaged in rhombohedral graphene multilayers. Depending on their formation mechanism, these walls respond in distinct ways to external magnetic probes. Therefore, understanding their behaviors is critical to the interpretation of experimental results. In this work, we examine domain walls formed from strain-induced one-dimensional structural defects that separate domains with complementary rhombohedral stacking orders. We show that while transport across such domain walls is controlled by the valley degree of freedom, the coupling to a magnetic field is dictated by the momentum-space chirality encoded in the Hamiltonian. As a consequence, structural domain walls are rendered electronically opaque by an applied magnetic field, while intrinsic domain walls formed by spontaneous valley symmetry breaking are unstable in the presence of such an ordering field and can be eliminated. This dichotomy allows the two types of domain walls to be distinguished in a magnetotransport experiment.

title: Learning the Shared Latent Structure of Cryo-EM Inverse Problems
abstract: Understanding biomolecular function requires characterizing three-dimensional structure and conformational variability, for which cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) is a powerful tool. Cryo-EM produces noisy two-dimensional particle images in which molecular structure, particle pose, and imaging conditions are jointly encoded. Recovering biological information from these observations spans inverse problems including pose estimation, heterogeneity analysis, and reconstruction. These tasks are usually addressed independently despite shared protein structure and image formation, motivating a common representation across inverse problems. Since biologically meaningful differences may be spatially localized, we study self-distillation with complementary global and masked patch objectives. Because experimental dataset discrimination can reflect acquisition-specific cues, we develop controlled synthetic and experimental evaluations and find that structural discrimination benefits from dense spatial features. We introduce the EMber family of vision transformers, pre-trained on >50 million experimental particle images from 214 EMPIAR datasets together with simulated projections from 268,000 molecular assemblies. EMber improves upon existing methods at conformational and compositional discrimination by 14.85 and 14.26 percentage points, estimates conformational populations to within 1.59pp error with a linear probe, and produces particle assignments yielding reference-quality reconstructions in fewer epochs. We demonstrate how to learn representations that capture biological information for use across multiple cryo-EM inverse problems.

title: Iron Intermediates in Aminoquinoline-Directed C(sp2)–H Activation/C–C Coupling
abstract: Over the past two decades, iron-catalyzed aminoquinoline-directed C–H functionalization has attracted significant attention due to the low cost and sustainability of iron, the mild conditions required for catalysis, and the novel mechanistic manifolds compared to those with other first row metals. This report describes organometallic studies that provide insights into FeII, FeIII, and FeIV intermediates involved in an aminoquinoline-directed C(sp2)–H activation/C(sp2)–C(sp2) coupling reaction to yield a dimeric product.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Chiral Cartograph3R: A Quick Filtering Framework for Stereochemical Enumeration Integrating Chemistry Rules, 3D-Aware SDF Atom Mapping, Chirality Validation, and Spectral Geometry Features
abstract: Stereochemical enumeration pipelines often overproduce candidate structures that are topologically admissible yet chemically impossible, mechanistically implausible, or silently corrupted by atom-order mismatch between canonical molecular representations and three-dimensional embeddings. These failure modes become increasingly costly in workflows that must explore large stereochemical chemical spaces, preserve chirality, and feed candidates into expensive downstream quantum-chemical, docking, or machine-learning stages.

title: Rare earth element biosensing in chemically complex waters: Interference mechanisms, operating windows, and mitigation for a lanmodulin enzymatic switch
abstract: Rare earth elements (REE) are increasingly mobilised from mine residues and other industrial sources, creating a need for rapid screening of chemically complex waters where conventional ICP-based analysis is impractical on site. Here, we evaluate a lanthanide-gated enzymatic switch biosensor, for matrix-aware monitoring of mine-influenced waters. We quantified REE-dependent activation and systematic interference from co-occurring metals and anions typical of mine waters, and defined operating windows that preserve lanthanide responsiveness. REE activation was readily detectable at ~100 nM, whereas inhibition emerged in the low-micromolar range and became pronounced near ~10 µM for key interferents, corresponding to a practical tolerance of roughly 1:100 (REE:inhibiting element). Inhibition was strongest for AlIII, FeIII, GaIII, ZnII, and SnII. Combined machine learning, molecular dynamics, and density functional theory analyses indicate distinct inhibition modes, including coordination of FeIII, ZnII, and SnII at the LanM EF4 hand loop and favourable binding of [Al(OH)4]-/[Ga(OH)4]- near the TEM-1 substrate-recognition region. Consistent with these predictions, citrate reduced inhibition from hydrolysing metals, especially AlIII and SnII. Together, these findings define matrix-dependent operating envelopes, mechanistic design rules, and practical mitigation strategies for deploying REE biosensors in chemically complex waters.

title: Mechanical characterization of human centromeres
abstract: Centromeres must withstand high pulling forces in metaphase, yet allow rapid and complete chromosome segregation in anaphase. Using optical tweezers measurements on isolated human metaphase chromosomes, we find that centromeres are stiffer at low forces and more frequently exhibit pronounced softening compared to whole chromosomes, while displaying a similar stiffening response at high forces. We capture these mechanical properties by establishing a softened hierarchical worm-like chain model. Cohesin cleavage alters the mechanical properties of centromeres but does not lead to chromosome segregation in vitro. Topoisomerase II is recruited to centromeric regions under significant tension, likely to resolve the persistent centromeric DNA entanglements that provide additional sister chromatid cohesion. These findings advance our understanding of the mechanical resilience and regulation of centromeres during mitosis.

title: A Restricted No-Go Theorem for Exact, Coherent, and Isolated Quantum Learning Architectures
abstract: The straightforward translation of classical machine learning models into the quantum domain is obstructed by fundamental structural constraints of quantum mechanics. In this work, we rigorously examine the interplay between universality, coherent training, and isolation in quantum learning systems. We prove a restricted no-go theorem: within the setting of exact continuous unitary hypothesis classes, finite-dimensional closed quantum systems, and fully coherent parameter-update rules with no intermediate measurement or classical feedback, no architecture can simultaneously satisfy…

title: Tailoring Dynamic Cu Redox Responsiveness via Pr-Modified Ceria for Enhanced Reverse Water–Gas Shift
abstract: The reverse water–gas shift (RWGS) reaction is a key technology for converting CO2 into CO as a versatile intermediate for chemical production. Among various catalysts, Cu/CeO2 has attracted considerable attention owing to its high CO selectivity, yet its activity is affected by the oxidation and reduction behavior of Cu under reaction conditions. Although rare-earth modification has been widely employed to improve the redox properties of ceria, the relationship between support modification and the dynamic Cu redox behavior during RWGS remains poorly understood.

title: Long Noncoding RNA: An Uncharted Territory in Plant Diseases and Immunity
abstract: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) are a class of transcripts longer than 200 nucleotides with little or no protein-coding capacity. They represent a substantial fraction of eukaryotic genomes and function as molecular architects that coordinate diverse biological processes and physiological plasticity, including multilayered plant defence systems, through versatile regulatory interactions at multiple levels of gene regulation.

title: Clinical characteristics and risk factors for intensive care unit admission and mortality in rapid response team-activated ward patients: a retrospective cohort study at a tertiary hospital in South Korea
abstract: BackgroundFactors driving intensive care unit (ICU) transfer decisions and mortality after rapid response team (RRT) activation remain unclear. We identified independent predictors of ICU admission, 28-day mortality, and in-hospital mortality in RRT-activated ward patients.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included adults with first RRT activation from September 2023 to August 2025 at a Korean tertiary hospital (n=549). Multivariable logistic regression with backward elimination was used.ResultsOf 549 patients, 191 (34.8%) were transferred to the ICU.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Simultaneous Synthesis and Segmentation Via Evidential Deep Learning
abstract: Daily anatomical changes during radiotherapy demand accurate imaging and segmentation to support adaptive treatment. We propose Simultaneous Evidential Network for Synthesis and SEgmentation (SENSSE), a deep learning framework that jointly performs synthetic CT generation and anatomical segmentation from daily CBCT or MR images, while also estimating voxel-wise uncertainty.
venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics

title: Tetrapyridophenazine-Based Vinylene-Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks for Efficient Sequential Photocatalysis and Continuous-Flow Synthesis
abstract: Vinylene-linked covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising photocatalysts because their conjugated sp2-carbon frameworks combine exceptional chemical stability with efficient charge transport. However, the limited reversibility of C═C bond formation narrows the scope of polymerizable monomers, restricting the structural diversity and electronic tunability of vinylene-linked COFs. Here, we report a molecular design strategy based on a planar, electron-deficient, nitrogen-rich tetrapyridophenazine (TTPhz) building block for constructing vinylene-linked COFs.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Early-warning evaluation of pasteurized milk spoilage during storage and distribution.
abstract: Hidden temperature deviations within the cold chain are a major contributor to global food waste, yet existing quality assurance methods predominantly rely on lagging indicators that fail to capture early-stage spoilage. Here, we integrate high-resolution foodomics with machine learning approaches to identify a biomarker for pasteurized milk freshness: N-((4-amino-2-methylpyrimidin-5-yl)methyl)formamide (AMF). Through structural elucidation and isotope tracing, we revealed that AMF is formed via a specific hydrolytic ring-opening pathway of thiamine.

title: Precise prediction of amino acid content and geographical origin tracing of lotus seeds based on multimodal data fusion and Bayesian optimization
abstract: This study established a three-tiered framework of feature characterization, information coupling and modeling mapping to correlate multi-source coupled information with the geographical origin and quality of lotus seeds. Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS), gray level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) texture features and amino acid profiles were acquired, and Bayesian optimization was adopted. Dual-modal (amino acid + NIRS; amino acid + GLCM) and tri-modal (amino acid + NIRS + GLCM) models were constructed.

title: Time-of-Flight Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry for Characterization of Ir-Based Catalysts for PEM Water Electrolyzers
abstract: Iridium-based catalysts remain essential for enabling durable oxygen evolution in proton-exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs), yet their surface and subsurface chemistries remain insufficiently resolved by conventional characterization methods. Here, we establish time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry (ToF-SIMS), combined with multivariate analysis, as a framework for deconvoluting chemical-, structural-, and depth-dependent features across commercial IrOx powders spanning amorphous and rutile phases.

title: Uncovered: Cities of chemistry
abstract: C&EN staffers dig into an interactive data piece about where chemistry happens
authors: Jeremy Barr, special to C&EN, Craig Bettenhausen, Rowan Walrath, Shea Murphy

title: The Signaling Pathway of a Bacterial Two-Component System Determined by cryo-EM
abstract: Although two-component systems (TCSs) play ubiquitous roles in sensing signals for bacterial survival and virulence, a detailed structural map of the signal transduction pathway is lacking. Bacteriophytochromes (BphPs) are enzymatic photoreceptors with homologs in plants that regulate bacterial physiological responses via TCS signaling. Here, we employ cryo-EM to elucidate the structural basis of a light-regulated TCS by capturing the full-length BphP histidine kinase (HK) in complex with its downstream response regulator (RR). The RR binds as a dimer to the HK but contacts the enzyme only through one subunit. Light absorption perturbs the entire BphP structure, including the HK domain, which disrupts phosphorylation and phosphotransfer reactions and promote TCS complex dissociation. Thus, light controls signaling through both HK activity and reversible binding of the RR.

title: High-Resolution X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy of Soluble Methane Monooxygenase: Room Temperature and Cryogenic Insights into Active Site Electronic Structure Modulation
abstract: Room temperature HERFD XAS (High Energy Resolution Fluorescence Detected X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy) data collected on the stable Fe(III)Fe(III) (ox) and Fe(II)Fe(II) (red) states of the soluble methane monooxygenase hydroxylase (sMMOH) from Methylosinus trichosporium (Mt) OB3b using laminar flow cells reveal structural differences with varied temperature, pH, and presence of regulatory protein MMOB. High quality room-temperature data on the X-ray radiation sensitive MMOH-ox:MMOB state shows two distinct radiative reduction events, confirming the presence of a so-called semimet (Fe(II)Fe(III)) state in Mt sMMO, and for the first time presents the undamaged HERFD XAS spectra of MMOH-ox and MMOH-ox:MMOB. Clear differences in the whiteline and pre-edge of MMOH-red:MMOB appear between room temperature and cryogenic data, indicating the presence of cryogenic artifacts. In light of this new room temperature data, TD-DFT calculations based on optimized QM/MM models have been used to assign the structures of MMOH-red and ox states. MMOH-red and MMOH-red:MMOB have been assigned as 6,6-coordinate on the basis of pre-edge intensities, with minor perturbations in the ligand field seen upon MMOB binding. MMOH-ox:MMOB and MMOH-ox have been assigned as 6,6-coordinate with different protonation states at pH 7 on the basis of calculated models and changes in the experimental pre-edge energies and intensities for MMOH-ox:MMOB at pH 7.5. Together these results establish a revised structural and mechanistic framework for sMMO and demonstrate the potential of microfluidic HERFD XAS for capturing authentic enzymatic states.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Structure-Based Design with Arylazopyrazoles to Enable High-Affinity Photoswitchable Inhibitors of N -Myristoyltransferase
abstract: Photopharmacology using photoswitches is a powerful way to reversibly control biological function with light, through the generation of photoswitchable synthetic ligands. While optimization of bioactive small molecules is increasingly driven by iterative experimental protein–ligand structures, structure-guided improvement in photoswitch photopharmacology using experimental structures remains rare. Here we report the development of the first photoswitchable inhibitors of the human enzyme N-myristoyltransferase 1 (HsNMT1), using an arylazopyrazole (AAP) as the switch motif. Through experimental structure-based design, we obtain inhibitors with single-digit nanomolar affinity for NMT, functional activity in cells, and good differential activity between E and Z photoswitch isomers. The availability of our highly potent ligands and protein–ligand structures, coupled with the excellent photoswitch properties of the AAP, allowed us to study the effect of protein binding on the switching events, including characterization of protein-bound Z → E photoisomerization kinetics for the first time. Overall, this study showcases the potential for structure-based design in photoswitch pharmacology, including understanding the dynamic consequences of target binding, paving the way for the development of advanced photopharmaceuticals.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: From Algebraic Completeness to Orbit Separation: Recursive Separating Invariants for Global Neural Network Potential Energy Surfaces
abstract: Permutationally invariant polynomials (PIPs) provide a systematically improvable, symmetry-preserving representation for global potential energy surfaces (PESs), but their high computational cost as neural network descriptors limits applications to large molecular systems. Fundamental invariants (FIs), which form an algebraically complete generating set, substantially reduce the number of descriptors and enable neural network PESs for larger systems. However, PES evaluation remains computationally expensive as molecular size and complexity increase. Here, we introduce recursive separating invariants (RSIs), shifting the descriptor design principle from algebraic completeness to orbit separation. RSIs are constructed systematically through correlation order and recursion depth, providing a more computationally efficient representation. Benchmarks on reactive and nonreactive systems demonstrate that RSI-based neural network (RSI-NN) PESs achieve approximately an order-of-magnitude faster evaluation than their FI-NN counterparts, with system-dependent prediction accuracy that is comparable in several cases. These results establish orbit separation as a promising principle for developing efficient symmetry-preserving descriptors for global neural network PESs.

title: Correlation between normal character and Raman intensities of isotopologues of carbon dioxide
abstract: Previous studies on the vibrational structure of carbon dioxide isotopologues have revealed a correlation between the strength of Fermi interactions and a recently defined normal-mode parameter. In this contribution, we investigate how the Raman intensities of the most intense bands evolve across the complete series of carbon dioxide isotopologues at room temperature. To this end, we introduce a general scheme for simulating Raman intensities in linear triatomic molecules, based on the computation of the mean polarizability surface up to cubic terms for all twelve stable species. For the first time, we establish correlations between the degree of normality and the Raman transition intensities, mean polarizability derivatives, and variational Raman shift errors across the CO$_2$ isotopologue series. The observed trends are further analyzed by considering rotational contributions, which may partially account for the deviations observed in the correlations. Our study is supported by experimental Raman spectra of isotopically enriched samples and theoretical simulations. Although this study focuses on carbon dioxide, similar behavior is expected for other series of isotopologues.

title: Bond-informed search for ordered configurations in multi-principal element alloys
abstract: Ordered configurations in multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) control their local structure and influence a broad range of mechanical and thermodynamic properties. Yet they are notoriously difficult to identify. Locating low-energy ordered candidates requires exploring a configurational space that grows combinatorially with the number of elements, and Monte Carlo searches driven by density-functional theory (DFT) need a new electronic-structure calculation at every trial step. Here we introduce MECx (Minimum Energy Configuration eXplorer), a framework that guides Monte Carlo searches with a surrogate energy model trained on configurations stratified in bond-count space. Applied to ternary, quaternary, and quinary BCC alloys using compact training sets of 100 DFT-labeled configurations, MECx identifies ordered configurations with lower energies than those found by direct DFT-based Monte Carlo within practical computational limits. These configurations exhibit distinct pair-specific ordering, including B2- and B32-like motifs, and undergo progressive disordering as temperature increases. The MPEA-trained models also transfer to selected binary subsystems without retraining. The resulting ordered configurations agree with those obtained by direct DFT-based Monte Carlo and produce experimentally distinguishable superlattice reflections in simulated neutron diffraction patterns.

title: Low magnon damping of a EuSe film down to millikelvin temperatures
abstract: The rapid development of quantum magnonics over the past decade has created a demand for magnetic materials that keep their magnon losses low at millikelvin temperatures and add functionality beyond that of the established iron garnets and ferromagnetic metals. The europium chalcogenides are natural candidates $-$ they are magnetic semiconductors whose moment of $7\,μ_{\mathrm{B}}$ per Eu$^{2+}$ ion stems from a half-filled $4f$ shell with zero orbital momentum, so that spin-orbit coupling and intrinsic damping are expected to be weak. Here we characterize an epitaxial film of the metamagnet EuSe on diamagnetic BaF$_2$ by magnetometry and broadband ferromagnetic resonance from 10 K down to 30 mK. EuSe combines a saturation magnetization of 1100 kA/m with antiferromagnetic, ferrimagnetic and ferromagnetic phases that are reached with fields below 0.25 T. In contrast to a Gilbert-damped ferromagnet, the linewidth of the field-aligned film decreases with increasing frequency and field, and below 750 mK it no longer depends on temperature. At 30 mK, 68 GHz and 1.8 T, it reaches 5.5 mT, close to the values of bulk single crystals, which corresponds to a magnon lifetime of 2 ns and to an upper bound of $1.1\times10^{-3}$ for the Gilbert damping parameter. These properties make EuSe and the europium chalcogenides promising materials for hybrid quantum systems and quantum magnonics.

title: DeciCAD: Harness-Grounded Learning of Action Policies for CAD Agents
abstract: Large Language Model agents operate through closed-loop action policies whose decision space is defined by an agent harness. We investigate how this operating space shapes agent behavior and policy learning in computer-aided design (CAD), a professional domain characterized by persistent state, geometric constraints, and long-horizon procedures. We instantiate this perspective in DeciCAD, a domain-native harness that exposes semantic CAD actions, decision-oriented observations, environment feedback, and persistent state transitions. Building on this harness, we develop a learning pipeline that extracts causal decision supervision from interaction trajectories and improves the policy through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and geometry-grounded online reinforcement learning (RL). Across four CAD benchmarks, DeciCAD achieves the best F1 and intersection over union (IoU) while reducing model-output tokens by 45--88% relative to a general-purpose coding harness. Under matched supervision, its SFT policy improves F1 from 0.6883 to 0.7437 and outperforms the coding policy; subsequent online RL further raises geometry availability from 66.5% to 73.5% and F1 to 0.7880. These results demonstrate that the decision space induced by a harness materially affects both agent execution and policy learning in CAD.

title: Hierarchical universal open structure dataset for atomistic modeling
abstract: Atomic-scale simulations have been transformed by machine-learning models that predict the properties of atomistic structures with the accuracy of quantum calculations, but at a small fraction of the cost. These models have increased dramatically in generality, thanks to the availability of synthetic datasets of ever-increasing size and scope. The proliferation of datasets, with properties often computed using different levels of electronic-structure approximation, is problematic, as there is often overlap between different datasets, and strong correlations between structures obtained with short molecular dynamics trajectories or geometry optimization.
